standard.title: Department of Defense Design Criteria Standard: Human Engineering
standard.distribution: Distribution Statement A: approved for public release; distribution is unlimited.
standard.page_numbers: Printed page numbers of the standard (PDF page = printed page + 17).

about: Requirements of MIL-STD-1472H that the website could check or report, extracted from the 456-page standard, including the dimensional tables that are printed only as figures. 'text' is a close paraphrase with every number and unit as printed; check the standard itself before you rely on a value for a compliance claim. See README.md.

fields.id: Stable identifier built from the paragraph and title.
fields.para: Paragraph number, or the table/figure that holds the limit.
fields.checkable: auto (computable from the scene, mannequin or posture) | semi (computable once the user enters a value the site lacks, e.g. force, frequency, control type) | manual (yes/no checklist item) | na (not applicable to the website)
fields.category: Short topic tag (stairs, ladder, console, lifting, rom, ...).
fields.values: List of {quantity, min, max, preferred, unit, condition}; some tables carry extra structured keys. 'misprint': true marks a limit kept exactly as printed although the standard's own numbers are inconsistent (e.g. min > max).
fields.site_hook: How the website would check it, or which object or parameter it needs.
fields.percentile_rule: The accommodation rule the item names (e.g. central 90 percent per sex), or null.

requirements.title: Anthropometric accommodation (definition)
requirements.text: Having sufficient reach, movement, clearance, and visibility to safely perform all required tasks while wearing the appropriate mission ensemble and equipment; includes clearance for movement, ingress/egress of work areas, internal and external visibility, and reach and actuation of controls through their full range of travel.
requirements.site_hook: Defines the four checks the site should run per task: reach, clearance, visibility, ingress/egress.

requirements.title: Central 90 percent accommodation (definition)
requirements.text: Multivariate central 90 percent of suitably clothed and equipped males and of females; the 10 percent not accommodated should be split evenly between the small and large ends; multivariate methods are required when several measures must be accommodated at once; univariate accommodation can use the 5th to 95th percentiles of a single dimension.
requirements.site_hook: Univariate: P5..P95 of the governing dimension per sex. Multivariate: count ANSUR II individuals (and other open datasets) that pass all relevant dimension checks at once.
requirements.percentile_rule: 5th-95th per sex (univariate); multivariate central 90% per sex otherwise

requirements.title: Accommodation (general rule)
requirements.text: Unless otherwise specified, equipment, systems and subsystems shall accommodate the multivariate central 90 percent (95 percent preferred) of suitably clothed and equipped males and the multivariate central 90 percent (95 percent preferred) of suitably clothed and equipped females of the target user population.
requirements.site_hook: Default boundary for every anthropometric check: P5 female .. P95 male (univariate) or multivariate 90% per sex; 'preferred' level P2.5..P97.5.
requirements.percentile_rule: central 90% (95% preferred) of males AND of females

requirements.title: Accommodation rule (general)
requirements.text: Unless otherwise specified elsewhere in this standard or by the procuring activity, equipment, systems, and subsystems shall be designed to accommodate both the multivariate central 90 percent (95 percent preferred) of suitably clothed and equipped males of the target user population, and the multivariate central 90 percent (95 percent preferred) of suitably clothed and equipped females of the target user population.
requirements.site_hook: Global compliance rule: run every geometric check for a mannequin family spanning the central 90% (95% preferred) of each sex; site can approximate with P5F..P95M (or P2.5F..P97.5M) univariate cases, better with a multivariate boundary-case set (e.g. PCA ellipse cases from ANSUR II) plus clothing/equipment increments
requirements.percentile_rule: multivariate central 90% (95% preferred) of males and of females, clothed and equipped

requirements.title: Design factors: space, access, clothing compatibility
requirements.text: Design should reflect, when applicable: (d) space for personnel, their equipment, and free volume for movements during operation and maintenance under normal, adverse, and emergency conditions; (i) passageways, hatches, ladders, stairways, platforms, inclines and other provisions for ingress, egress and passage; (j) body support and restraint, seating; (p) compatibility of the design, location and layout of controls, displays, workspaces, maintenance accesses, stowage provisions, passenger compartments and control movements with the clothing and personal equipment to be worn.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist; supports adding clothing/equipment increments (helmet, body armour, CBRN, arctic) to mannequin dimensions for clearance checks

requirements.title: Crew-served interaction
requirements.text: The design of the system shall reflect the interaction requirements of crew-served equipment.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist; multi-mannequin scenes could show crew positions

requirements.title: Fall protection: elevated work height threshold
requirements.text: Design shall provide protection or prevention of falls from elevated work surfaces in accordance with ANSI/ASSP Z359. Design shall limit risk of fall from elevated work locations, considered to be 4 feet in general industry and 5 feet in maritime industry, through a hierarchy of controls (eliminate, fixed barriers such as handrails, aerial lifts/scaffolding, administrative controls). When fixed barriers are not feasible, designs shall provide a personal fall arrest system.
requirements.site_hook: Sandbox platform/work surface height: flag fall-protection need (guardrail/handrail object) when standing surface height >= 4 ft (1.22 m) general or 5 ft (1.52 m) maritime

requirements.title: Fall protection: anchor points and fall clearance
requirements.text: Fall prevention programs include: (b) certified anchor points (5,000-pound [lb] test) for harnesses in accessible locations; (c) certified full-body harnesses (belts shall not be used except for positioning); (d) fall distance calculation accommodating lanyard expansion plus allowance for height of the person (typically 15 feet [ft] total); (f) anchor points placed so the individual will not pendulum into harm's way.

values.quantity: total fall clearance (lanyard expansion + person height)

requirements.site_hook: Could check clearance below an elevated platform >= 15 ft (4.57 m) when fall arrest is the control; anchor rating is manual

requirements.title: Personal fall arrest system limits
requirements.text: A personal fall arrest system includes an approved full-body harness and equipment providing controlled expansion that limits the impact forces on the victim (to 1,800 pounds) and certified anchorages (> 3,600 lbs).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist / info only

requirements.title: CBRNE PPE compatibility
requirements.text: As applicable, equipment design shall be compatible with CBRNE, directed energy, or other mission-required PPE.
requirements.site_hook: Add PPE clothing ensemble option (mask, hood, gloves, overboots) that increments mannequin dimensions and reduces ROM; re-run reach/clearance checks

requirements.title: Mission-essential operations in CBRNE PPE
requirements.text: Equipment design shall permit performance of mission-essential operations, communications, maintenance, resupply, and decontamination tasks by suitably clothed, trained, and acclimatized personnel for the survival periods and CBRNE environments specified.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist; PPE mannequin variant for reach/clearance

requirements.title: Anthropometric accommodation of PPE
requirements.text: Anthropometric accommodation and design of CBRNE, directed energy protection, or other mission-required PPE systems shall be in accordance with section 5.8.
requirements.site_hook: Cross-reference to 5.8 anthropometry; use survey data for PPE sizing
requirements.percentile_rule: per 5.8

requirements.title: Colour-deficient users
requirements.text: Colors used for functional purposes (visual displays, controls, workspaces, equipment connections) shall accommodate users with color-deficient vision.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist; optionally simulate colour-deficient view of a display object

requirements.title: Aircrew systems
requirements.text: Aircrew systems shall be designed as specified (see 6.2). Refer to JSSG-2010 for further guidance; additional aircrew system design guidance in MIL-DTL-7788.
requirements.site_hook: Reference only; pilot postures exist but limits come from JSSG-2010

requirements.title: Ejection acceleration limits
requirements.text: For guidance on exposure to short-duration (less than one second), linear and angular acceleration during ejection seat operation, see ADV-PUB-4048. Parachute-opening acceleration after seat separation is excluded.
requirements.site_hook: No numeric limit in 1472H; refers to ADV-PUB-4048

requirements.title: Crash protection references
requirements.text: For occupant crash protection and crash-protective aspects of seating, restraint, crewstation and passenger/troop station design, see JSSG-2010-7 and USAAVSCOM TR 89-D-22 (A through E), Aircraft Crash Survival Design Guide Volumes 1 through 5.
requirements.site_hook: Reference only

requirements.title: Escape and egress systems
requirements.text: For guidance on escape and egress systems, see MIL-HDBK-516.
requirements.site_hook: Reference only

requirements.title: Selection of mechanical controls (Table I / Table II)
requirements.text: Criteria in Table I should be used to choose the best type of mechanical control for control panels; Table II shows recommended controls by control function and actuation force (small vs large).
requirements.site_hook: New 'control' sandbox object with a control-type and function parameter; look up Table I preference rank (1/2/3) and Table II recommendation; report as advisory

requirements.title: Accommodation of user population (controls and motion envelopes)
requirements.text: Unless otherwise specified, the type of control selected and the location of the motion envelopes shall accommodate the multivariate central 90 percent (95 percent preferred) of suitably clothed and equipped males and the multivariate central 90 percent (95 percent preferred) of suitably clothed and equipped females of the target user population for body dimensions.
requirements.site_hook: Run reach check of each control object for a boundary set of mannequins (e.g., P5 female and P95 male, or multivariate boundary cases) and report pass/fail per control
requirements.percentile_rule: multivariate central 90% (95% preferred) of clothed/equipped males and of females of target population

requirements.title: Two-dimensional design elements: percentiles
requirements.text: Fifth percentile strength values and 5th or 95th percentile univariate physical dimension values shall be used for two-dimensional design elements (see figures 22 and 23).
requirements.site_hook: Use P5/P95 single-dimension values from selected survey for 2-D layout checks; P5 strength for force limits
requirements.percentile_rule: 5th percentile strength; 5th or 95th percentile univariate dimensions

requirements.title: Handedness accommodation
requirements.text: Equipment design shall accommodate both right- and left-handed users.
requirements.site_hook: Mirror the mannequin (left-hand reach) and re-run reach checks for hand-operated controls

requirements.title: Handedness priority
requirements.text: If constraints permit only one group of users (right- or left-handed) to be accommodated, the majority of the target user population shall receive priority.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Compatibility with handwear
requirements.text: Controls shall be compatible with handwear to be utilized in the anticipated environment. Unless specified for glove use, all dimensions herein are for bare hands and shall be adjusted for use with gloves or mittens (see table VII).
requirements.site_hook: Add a 'handwear' parameter (bare/flash glove/heavy glove/arctic mitten) to control checks; apply glove adders from figures/tables

requirements.title: Distribution of workload across limbs
requirements.text: Controls should be selected and distributed so that none of the user's limbs will be overburdened.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item; could count controls assigned per limb

requirements.title: Multirotation controls
requirements.text: Multirotation controls should be used when precision is required over a wide range of adjustment.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Detent controls
requirements.text: Detent controls shall be selected whenever the operational mode requires control operation in discrete steps.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Stops
requirements.text: Stops shall be provided at the beginning and end of the range-of-control positions if the control is not to be operated beyond the indicated end positions or within specified limits.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Power assist feedback
requirements.text: Power assist may be used to reduce force inputs. When servo-amplifier devices are used, proportional resistance or force feedback shall be provided to give the feel of unpowered control.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Consistency of movement direction
requirements.text: Direction of control movement shall be consistent with related movement of an associated display, equipment component, or vehicle. In general, forward, clockwise, to the right, up, or pressing shall turn on, increase, or move forward/clockwise/right/up. Valve controls excluded.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item; could be a direction attribute on control objects

requirements.title: Multidimensional operation exception
requirements.text: When the vehicle/equipment may move in more than two dimensions, exception to 5.1.1.2.1 shall be made if needed to ensure consistency of anticipated response (e.g., forward stick causes descent).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Mechanical control criteria (preference by function)
requirements.text: Preference ranking (1 = most preferred, 2 = secondary, 3 = least) of selector switch, round knob, discrete thumbwheel, continuous thumbwheel, crank, push button, toggle switch, rocker switch, lever, joystick/lever/ball/mouse for each function. Examples: Select power ON-OFF: push button 1, lever 1a (heavy duty power circuits), toggle 2, rocker 2, selector 3. 3-state OFF-STBY-ON: selector 1, round knob 2, toggle 2, rocker 3. Select one of 3 to 24 discrete alternatives (sequential): selector switch 1. Set value on continuous scale: round knob 1, continuous thumbwheel 2, crank 3, lever 3. Enter alphanumeric data: push button (keyboard) 1. Initiate directional function: toggle 1, rocker 1d, lever 1, push button 2d, joystick/ball/mouse 2. Engage-disengage mechanical function: lever 1. Coarse adjustment: round knob (small diameter) 1; cont. thumbwheel (small motion) 2, crank (few turns) 2, lever (short throw) 2, joystick 2. Fine adjustment: round knob (large diameter) 1; cont. thumbwheel 2, crank (many turns) 2, lever (long throw) 3, joystick 2. Single-coordinate tracking: lever 1, crank 2, knob 3. Two-coordinate tracking: joystick/ball/mouse 1, crank 3.
requirements.site_hook: Lookup table keyed by function x control type; show rank when user tags a control object

requirements.title: Recommended manual controls by actuation force
requirements.text: Small actuation force: 2 discrete positions - key lock, legend switch, push button, slide switch, toggle switch; 3 discrete - push button, rotary selector, toggle; 4 to 24 discrete - rotary selector switch; continuous setting (linear and less than 360°) - continuous rotary knob, joystick or lever; continuous slewing and fine adjustment - continuous rotary knob, crank, joystick or lever. Large actuation force: 2 discrete - detent lever, foot push button, hand push button; 3 to 24 discrete - detent lever, rotary selector switch; continuous setting (linear and less than 360°) - crank, handwheel, joystick or lever, two-axis grip handle; continuous setting (greater than 360°) - crank, handwheel, two-axis grip handle, valve.
requirements.site_hook: Lookup table keyed by function and force class

requirements.title: Combined controls compatibility
requirements.text: When several controls are combined in one device, responses shall be compatible with control movement (e.g., right motion = clockwise roll, right turn, movement right).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: User-control orientation
requirements.text: Controls shall be oriented with respect to the user. Where a vehicle user may use two or more stations, controls shall cause movement oriented to the user at the effecting station unless remote visual reference is used.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Valve control direction
requirements.text: Rotary valve controls shall open the valve with a counterclockwise motion.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item / attribute of handwheel object

requirements.title: Labeling of valve controls
requirements.text: Valve controls shall be provided with double-ended arrows showing direction of operation and labeled at each end (e.g., open and close).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Ball valve controls
requirements.text: Ball valves with lever handles shall have valve position indication (open/closed) and double-ended arrows showing direction of operation.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Grouping of controls with displays
requirements.text: Controls operated in a task-driven sequence or together shall be grouped together along with their associated displays. Steps selected by one control shall be arranged by order of occurrence (5.1.1.3.1.1); unnecessary cycling through ON/OFF shall be avoided (5.1.1.3.1.2).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Sequential operation arrangement
requirements.text: Where sequential operations follow a fixed pattern, controls shall be arranged to facilitate operation (e.g., left-to-right/top-to-bottom).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Location of primary controls
requirements.text: The most important and frequently used controls (particularly rotary controls and those requiring fine settings) shall have the most favorable position for ease of reaching and grasping.
requirements.site_hook: User tags controls as primary; site checks they lie within the comfortable (not just maximum) reach zone of the P5 mannequin and near the hand's neutral position

requirements.title: Consistency of arrangement
requirements.text: Arrangement of functionally similar or identical primary controls shall be consistent from panel to panel and across systems.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Remote controls
requirements.text: Controls operated remote from the display/equipment/vehicle shall be arranged to facilitate direction-of-movement consistency.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Maintenance and adjustment controls
requirements.text: Controls used solely for maintenance and adjustment shall be covered during normal operation but readily accessible and visible when required.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Spacing between controls
requirements.text: Minimum spacing between controls shall comply with table III; spacing between a control and an adjacent obstruction per the figures referenced in table III. Minimum spacing shall be increased for gloves, mittens, or CBRNE or other mission-required PPE when such operation is a system requirement.
requirements.site_hook: Sandbox control objects with type; compute edge-to-edge distance between pairs and compare with Table III / per-type figure; apply glove increase

requirements.title: Minimum edge-to-edge separation between different mechanical control types
requirements.text: Minimum edge-to-edge separation (one-hand, bare-handed operation; push buttons not separated by barriers): toggle-push button 13 mm (0.5 in); toggle-continuous rotary 19 mm (0.75 in); toggle-rotary selector 19 mm (0.75 in); toggle-discrete thumbwheel 13 mm (0.5 in); push button-continuous rotary 13 mm (0.5 in); push button-rotary selector 13 mm (0.5 in); push button-discrete thumbwheel 13 mm (0.5 in); continuous rotary-rotary selector 25 mm (1 in); continuous rotary-discrete thumbwheel 19 mm (0.75 in); rotary selector-discrete thumbwheel 19 mm (0.75 in). Same-type pairs: toggle see figure 16; push buttons see figure 14; continuous rotary see figure 12 (as printed); rotary selector see figure 6; discrete thumbwheel see figure 8.

values.condition: toggle switch to push button (0.5 in); one hand, bare hand
toggle switch to continuous rotary control (0.75 in); one hand, bare hand
toggle switch to rotary selector switch (0.75 in); one hand, bare hand
toggle switch to discrete thumbwheel (0.5 in); one hand, bare hand
push button to continuous rotary control (0.5 in); one hand, bare hand
push button to rotary selector switch (0.5 in); one hand, bare hand
push button to discrete thumbwheel (0.5 in); one hand, bare hand
continuous rotary control to rotary selector switch (1 in); one hand, bare hand
continuous rotary control to discrete thumbwheel (0.75 in); one hand, bare hand
rotary selector switch to discrete thumbwheel (0.75 in); one hand, bare hand

requirements.site_hook: Pairwise edge distance between typed control objects on a panel; flag pairs below matrix value

requirements.title: Control interference
requirements.text: Size, shape, and location of controls shall ensure that operating any one control does not interfere with the use of other controls or other duties.
requirements.site_hook: Check hand/arm volume of mannequin while operating one control does not collide with other control objects

requirements.title: Emergency shutoff controls
requirements.text: Emergency shutoff controls shall be accessible, not hidden, located to prevent accidental activation, and positioned within easy reach of the user.
requirements.site_hook: Tag control as emergency; verify within reach envelope of P5 mannequin in operating posture (restrained if applicable)
requirements.percentile_rule: multivariate central 90% (95% preferred) of clothed/equipped males and of females of target population

requirements.title: Advantages/disadvantages of control coding modes
requirements.text: Table IV compares location, shape, size, mode of operation, labeling and color coding (visual/nonvisual identification, low illumination, glove use, extra space, etc.).
requirements.site_hook: Reference only

requirements.title: Consistent application of coding
requirements.text: Where coding differentiates controls, application of the code shall be uniform throughout the system and other systems the user operates.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Location coding: controls beside or behind user
requirements.text: When controls are beside or behind the user, they shall be a minimum of 250 mm (10 in) apart for location coding.

values.quantity: separation between location-coded controls beside/behind user

requirements.site_hook: Compute distance between control objects located lateral/behind the mannequin's frontal plane; flag if < 250 mm

requirements.title: Location coding: similar functions
requirements.text: Controls associated with similar functions shall be in the same relative location from workstation to workstation and panel to panel.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Size coding: number of sizes
requirements.text: No more than three different sizes shall be used to code controls for discrimination by absolute size.
requirements.site_hook: Count distinct sizes among size-coded control objects

requirements.title: Size coding: same function same size
requirements.text: Controls used for the same function on different items of equipment shall be the same size.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Size coding: knob diameter difference
requirements.text: When knob diameter is the coding parameter, differences between diameters shall be not less than 13 mm (0.5 in).
requirements.site_hook: Compare diameters of size-coded knob objects

requirements.title: Size coding: knob thickness difference
requirements.text: When knob thickness is the coding parameter, differences between thicknesses shall be not less than 10 mm (0.4 in).
requirements.site_hook: Compare thicknesses of size-coded knob objects

requirements.title: Shape coding criteria
requirements.text: Shape coding may be used for identification by feel. When used: coded feature shall not interfere with manipulation; shapes identifiable by hand and eye regardless of position/orientation; tactually identifiable with gloves; positively and non-reversibly attached to shafts (5.1.1.4.4.1.5); easily recognizable shapes for touch-alone knobs (figure 1) (5.1.1.4.4.1.6); clearly associated with intended function (5.1.1.4.4.1.7).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Number of shapes
requirements.text: Number of shapes to be identified by each user by absolute discrimination shall be not more than 10.
requirements.site_hook: Count distinct shape codes

requirements.title: Minimum dimensions for shape-coded controls
requirements.text: Minimum control dimensions when users must distinguish controls by shape alone: a. Height 13 mm (0.5 in) or larger; b. Width 13 mm (0.5 in) or larger; c. Depth 6.5 mm (0.25 in) or larger.
requirements.site_hook: Control knob object dimensions vs minima when shape-coded

requirements.title: Color coding limits
requirements.text: Colors shall not be the sole means of control coding. Not more than five colors shall be used (5.1.1.4.5.1). Controls shall be black (SAE AMS-STD-595 17038, 27038, 37038) or gray (26231 or 36231) (5.1.1.4.5.2). Coding colors limited to red 11105/21105, green 14187, orange-yellow 13538/23538/33538, white 17875/27875/37875, blue 15123 if absolutely necessary (5.1.1.4.5.3). No gloss finishes where glare/friction degrades performance or in darkened areas (5.1.1.4.5.4-5).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Blind operation separation
requirements.text: Where 'blind' operation is necessary, hand controls shall be shape coded, or separated from adjacent controls by at least 125 mm (5 in).

values.quantity: separation for blind-operated controls (if not shape coded)

requirements.site_hook: User flags control as blind-operated; compute distance to nearest control object

requirements.title: Prevention of accidental actuation: location and design
requirements.text: Controls shall be designed and located so they are not susceptible to being moved accidentally, particularly critical controls. Internal/hidden controls protected (5.1.1.7.2); protection shall not preclude operation within required time (5.1.1.7.3).
requirements.site_hook: Check that critical control objects are not inside swept volumes of mannequin during ingress/egress or other control operation

requirements.title: Methods of protection against accidental actuation
requirements.text: One or more of: a. locate/orient so user unlikely to strike it; b. recess/shield/barriers (control entirely contained within recess or barrier envelope); c. cover or guard (no safety or lock wire); d. interlock; e. movement resistance; f. lock against passing through positions; g. rotary action; h. spring-loaded depress-to-turn.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item; (b) could be geometric check that control does not protrude beyond barrier envelope

requirements.title: Weapon fire trigger protection
requirements.text: Weapon (or directed energy) fire trigger/switch shall be clearly labeled and physically protected; trigger shall be guarded positive-action requiring continuous intent (5.1.1.7.6). Dead man controls shall be used wherever user incapacity can produce a critical condition (5.1.1.7.7).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Feedback / time lag
requirements.text: No discernible time lag between system condition change and its display; unavoidable lag requires immediate feedback; feedback shall indicate actuation and response.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Hazardous operations
requirements.text: Critical position of a control initiating hazardous operations shall activate visible and audible warnings in the affected area; critical/emergency control dedicated to that function only.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Control location relative to display
requirements.text: A control shall be located adjacent to (normally below or to the right of) its associated display and positioned so that neither the control nor the hand normally used for setting the control will obscure the display.
requirements.site_hook: Link control to display objects; check control is below/right of display and that mannequin hand/arm at the control does not intersect the eye-to-display sight line

requirements.title: Control/display relationship apparent
requirements.text: Relationship of control to display shall be immediately apparent and unambiguous, through proximity, grouping, coding, framing, labeling (5.1.2.1.3); complexity/precision consistent with system and user ability (5.1.2.1.4-5).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: System response times (Table V)
requirements.text: Maximum system response times for real-time systems shall not exceed Table V: key response 0.1 s; key print 0.2 s; page turn 1.0 s; page scan 0.5 s; XY entry 0.2 s; pointing 0.2 s; sketching 0.2 s; local update 0.5 s; host update 2.0 s; file update 10 s; inquiry (simple) 2.0 s; inquiry (complex) 10 s; error feedback 0.2 s.
requirements.site_hook: Not geometric; could be a manual checklist

requirements.title: Information-system feedback and error management (summary)
requirements.text: 5.1.2.1.6.1-5.1.2.1.7.13: feedback on status, input confirmation, processing messages when response > 1 s, countdown when delay > 10 s, startup feedback, rejection reasons, error correction and checking, critical entry acknowledgement, etc. Software dialog items, summarized only.
requirements.site_hook: Out of scope for geometry; manual checklist at most

requirements.title: Control illumination adjustability
requirements.text: Adjustable illumination shall be provided for controls (including labels/markings) read in darkened conditions; continuously adjustable or at least 30 increments from full bright to full off; continuous intensity control from full bright to 0.02 percent of full bright and off.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Simultaneous access by multiple crew
requirements.text: If more than one crewmember must have simultaneous access to a group of controls or displays, each user shall have physical and visual access to all controls, displays and communication needed for assigned tasks.
requirements.site_hook: Place several mannequins at their stations; check each assigned control is within that mannequin's reach and each display within its line of sight/visual field

requirements.title: Functional grouping and sequence
requirements.text: Functionally related controls and displays shall be located close together in functional groups; groups ordered left-to-right (preferred) or top-to-bottom (5.1.2.2.1.1); more frequently used and most important groups in areas of easiest access (5.1.2.2.1.3).
requirements.site_hook: User tags groups and frequency; check frequent groups are in preferred reach/visual zone

requirements.title: Functional group outline: non-critical
requirements.text: Where functional group coding is specified and gray panels are used, non-critical functional groups shall be outlined with a black border measuring 1.5 mm (0.0625 in) (SAE AMS-STD-595/27038).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Functional group outline: critical
requirements.text: Panels involving emergency or extremely critical operations shall be outlined with a red border measuring 5 mm (0.1875 in) (SAE AMS-STD-595/21136) or designated by contrasting color pads; orange-yellow and black striped border under red lighting (5.1.2.2.1.4.4).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Consistency and no mirror images
requirements.text: Location of recurring functional groups and items shall be consistent panel to panel; mirror image arrangements shall not be used (5.1.2.2.1.5.1).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Maintenance control/display groups
requirements.text: Groups solely for maintenance shall be in positions of lesser access relative to operating groups.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Arrangement within groups
requirements.text: Within groups, controls/displays located by operational sequence or function; otherwise by importance or frequency with the most important/frequent in the most accessible locations. Horizontal display rows associated with horizontal controls; vertical columns with vertical controls (5.1.2.2.3.2, 5.1.2.2.3.4); if fewer control rows, top-row display controls at left (5.1.2.2.3.3).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Simultaneous use: viewing angle
requirements.text: A visual display that must be monitored while a related control is manipulated shall be located so the user is not required to observe the display from an extreme visual angle (to maintain legibility and avoid parallax).
requirements.site_hook: With the mannequin's hand on the control, measure angle between eye-to-display line and display normal; flag large angles (see 5.2 limits; figure 2 shows instrument face at minimum 45° to normal line of sight)

requirements.title: Control for multiple displays
requirements.text: If one control requires reading several displays, the control shall be as near as possible to them and preferably beneath the middle of the displays, not obscuring them. Rotary selector sequence corresponds to displays; OFF position most counterclockwise; unselected displays read off-scale (5.1.2.2.3.6.1-3).
requirements.site_hook: Compute horizontal offset of control from centroid of linked displays; occlusion check

requirements.title: Combined (ganged) control placement
requirements.text: Displays affected by a combined control shall be arranged left to right with the combined control underneath the center of the displays, not obscuring them.

requirements.title: Display remains visible
requirements.text: Controls shall be located so the user's hand or arm does not obscure the associated display.
requirements.site_hook: Ray-cast from mannequin eye to linked display while hand is at control; flag occlusion by hand/forearm

requirements.title: Separated control and display panels
requirements.text: When controls are on panels separate from their displays, the panels shall be adjacent and mounted at approximately the same direction relative to the user; preferred display panel above control panel; not mounted facing each other; control positions correspond to display positions.
requirements.site_hook: Compare panel normals/orientation; check display panel above control panel

requirements.title: Component group orientation
requirements.text: Control/display positions shall correspond to controlled components (e.g., aircraft engine controls oriented for user facing normal direction of motion).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Emergency displays and controls location
requirements.text: Emergency displays and controls shall be located where they can be seen and reached without delay; e.g., warning lights should be within a 30-degree cone about the user's normal line of sight (median gaze direction) (figure 2).

values.quantity: cone about normal line of sight for warning lights

requirements.site_hook: Compute angle between normal line of sight (15° below horizontal per figure 2) and eye-to-warning-light vector; flag if outside 15° half-angle; reach check for emergency controls

requirements.title: Lines of sight
requirements.text: Figure 2: normal line of sight is 15° below the horizontal line of sight (0°); instrument face at minimum 45° to the normal line of sight.

values.quantity: normal line of sight below horizontal
instrument face angle to normal line of sight

requirements.site_hook: Use mannequin eye point; define normal LOS 15° down; compute display face angle to LOS and compare to minimum 45°

requirements.title: Emergency control proximity
requirements.text: An emergency control should be close to either its related warning display or the nearest available hand in its nominal operating position.
requirements.site_hook: Distance from emergency control to linked warning display and to mannequin hand in operating posture

requirements.title: Correspondence with equipment arrangement
requirements.text: Arrangement of controls/displays shall correspond to physical arrangement of associated units.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Control-display movement relationships
requirements.text: Display response consistent and predictable; no discernible lag; clockwise/forward/up/right control produces clockwise pointer and increase (moving pointer circular); tape scales larger value at top/right; fixed-pointer circular scales avoided; digital displays increase; rotary control if indicator arc > 180 degrees, linear allowed if < 180 degrees; indicator light arrays bottom-to-top or left-to-right increase (5.1.2.3.1-5.1.2.3.16).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Normal line of sight and minimum instrument-face angle
requirements.text: Figure 2 (Lines of sight): the normal line of sight is 15 degrees below the horizontal line of sight (0 degrees); the instrument face shall be at a minimum of 45 degrees to the normal line of sight.

values.quantity: normal line of sight below horizontal
angle between instrument face and normal line of sight

requirements.site_hook: Define the normal line of sight as a ray from the mannequin eye point 15 deg below horizontal (in the head frame or the world frame for an upright head); use it as reference for all display-angle checks

requirements.title: Knob coarse setting C/D ratio
requirements.text: One complete turn of a coarse-setting knob shall move the display element two-thirds the total length of the linear scale.
requirements.site_hook: User enters C/D ratio

requirements.title: Knob fine setting C/D ratio
requirements.text: For fine setting on linear scales, one complete turn shall move the display element between one-tenth and one-fifth of the total scale length.
requirements.site_hook: User enters C/D ratio

requirements.title: Bracketing arc
requirements.text: When bracketing, the control knob shall swing through an arc of not less than 10 degrees or more than 30 degrees on either side of the target value.
requirements.site_hook: User parameter

requirements.title: Lever coarse setting ratio
requirements.text: One unit of display-element movement shall be induced by three units of lever movement (coarse settings). Two-dimensional coarse settings: two and one-half units of lever movement per unit display movement (5.1.2.4.7).
requirements.site_hook: User parameter

requirements.title: Counter knob ratio
requirements.text: One revolution of a counter knob shall produce approximately 50 counts.
requirements.site_hook: User parameter

requirements.title: Touchscreen not sole input for high-frequency data entry or vibration
requirements.text: A touchscreen should not be the sole input means if used to enter large amounts of data frequently, or if movement/vibration might degrade performance (5.1.3.1.1.2). It shall not be the sole input device for mission-critical or safety-critical interfaces (5.1.3.1.1.3).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Touchscreen luminance transmission
requirements.text: Touchscreens shall have sufficient luminance transmission to be clearly readable in the intended environment (including from the seated position for the full range of users) and meet 5.2.1.2.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Touchscreen display latency
requirements.text: Display response time should not be more than 100 milliseconds (ms).
requirements.site_hook: Not geometric

requirements.title: Touchscreen critical tasks
requirements.text: Critical touchscreen actions shall require an additional confirmatory action; if impractical, multiple touch actuations (5.1.3.1.7.1). Positive indication of actuation (5.1.3.1.3).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Touchscreen repeat function delay
requirements.text: An initial delay of 500 to 750 ms shall be provided when a repeat delay is provided.
requirements.site_hook: Not geometric

requirements.title: Touchscreen sensitivity with gloves
requirements.text: Fingertip contact shall actuate; sensitivity shall match all operational modes including use of gloves.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Touchscreen parallax and glare mounting
requirements.text: Touchscreen devices shall be mounted to minimize parallax issues and specular glare.
requirements.site_hook: Compute eye-to-screen angle vs. screen normal; glare requires light source positions

requirements.title: Touchscreen viewing angle
requirements.text: When possible, touchscreens shall be perpendicular to the user's line of sight in the normal operating position. A reduced viewing angle, less than 90 degrees from horizontal, may reduce arm fatigue; changes shall be evaluated for parallax, glare and readability.

values.quantity: angle between line of sight and screen surface

requirements.site_hook: Sandbox display object flagged as touchscreen: compute angle between mannequin eye-to-screen-center vector and screen normal; report deviation from perpendicular

requirements.title: Touchscreen reach accommodation
requirements.text: Touchscreens shall be mounted to accommodate the multivariate central 90 percent (95 percent preferred) of suitably clothed and equipped males and females. Unless otherwise specified, users shall be able to reach and actuate all areas of the screen, including corners of the display.
requirements.site_hook: Reach targets at the four screen corners and centre for P5 female (and P95 male for clearance); IK fingertip reach must reach every corner
requirements.percentile_rule: multivariate central 90% (95% preferred) of clothed/equipped males and of females of target population

requirements.title: Touchscreen: avoid full arm extension
requirements.text: Touchscreens shall be located to avoid full arm extension.
requirements.site_hook: Check elbow angle from IK when fingertip is at farthest screen corner; flag near-full extension (e.g., elbow > ~160° or reach > ~90% of max reach)

requirements.title: Touchscreen emergency controls with harness locked
requirements.text: Emergency controls on touchscreens shall be reachable by crewmembers with harness or seat belt locked even if full arm extension is necessary.
requirements.site_hook: Restrained-reach check: lock torso/shoulder joints (no trunk flexion) and test fingertip reach to emergency target areas

requirements.title: Touchscreen: avoid upward reach
requirements.text: Touchscreens shall be located to avoid upward reach.
requirements.site_hook: Flag if any screen area is above the mannequin's shoulder height (or requires shoulder flexion above horizontal)

requirements.title: Touchscreen elbow support
requirements.text: Where possible, elbow support shall be provided to minimize arm fatigue.
requirements.site_hook: Check presence of armrest/console surface near elbow in operating posture

requirements.title: Touchscreen sustained interaction
requirements.text: Touchscreens shall not be used for frequent actions over extended duration (e.g., typing on a virtual keyboard); not applicable to small hand-held devices. May be used for intermittent actions (5.1.3.1.15). Color coding redundant (5.1.3.1.16).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Touchscreen target size, separation, resistance
requirements.text: Alphanumeric/numeric keyboards: actuation area A preferred 16 x 16 mm (0.6 x 0.6 in); separation S minimum 0, preferred 2 mm (0.08 in), maximum 6 mm (0.25 in); resistance minimum 250 mN (0.9 oz), maximum 1.5 N (5.3 oz). Other applications: A minimum 15 x 15 mm (0.6 x 0.6 in), maximum 38 x 38 mm (1.5 x 1.5 in); S minimum 3 mm (0.12 in), maximum 6 mm (0.25 in); resistance minimum 250 mN (0.9 oz), maximum 1.5 N (5.3 oz). Dimensions for ungloved finger touch. For Navy flash gloves add 5 mm (0.2 in) to each dimension of A. 'First contact' strategy: separation not less than 5 mm (0.2 in); 'last contact' strategy: may be less than 5 mm but not less than 3 mm (0.12 in) for applications other than alphanumeric/numeric keyboards.
requirements.site_hook: Touchscreen object parameter: target size & spacing (or per-target list); compare against Figure 3; physical screen size also usable to check target sizes given screen resolution

requirements.title: Keyboard layout
requirements.text: Alphanumeric keyboards and numeric keypads shall be in accordance with ANSI/HFES 100; keyboards shall be used for alphanumeric entry (5.1.3.2.1).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Keyboard key dimensions, resistance, displacement, separation
requirements.text: Key size (square): bare hand min 10 mm (0.4 in), preferred 13 mm (0.5 in), max 19 mm (0.75 in); arctic mittens (trigger finger type) min 19 mm (0.75 in), preferred 19 mm (0.75 in); Navy flash gloves min 15 mm (0.6 in), preferred 18 mm (0.7 in). Resistance: numeric min 1 N (3.5 oz), max 4 N (14 oz); alphanumeric min 0.25 N (0.9 oz), preferred 0.5 to 0.6 N (1.8 to 2.2 oz), max 1.5 N (5.3 oz); dual function min 0.25 N (0.9 oz), max 1.5 N (5.3 oz). Displacement: numeric 0.8-4.8 mm (0.03-0.19 in); alphanumeric 1.3-6.3 mm (0.05-0.25 in); dual function 0.8-4.8 mm (0.03-0.19 in). Separation between adjacent key tops min 6.4 mm (0.25 in), preferred 6.4 mm (0.25 in). Vehicle applications: dimensions bare hand 10-25 mm (0.4-1 in), gloved hand 19-25 mm (0.75-1 in); numeric input resistance 2.8-6.7 N (9.9-23.7 oz); separation preferred 13 mm (0.5 in). Membrane keys: preferred displacement 0.7 mm (0.03 in), resistance not less than 2.0 N (7.2 oz), positive tactile 'snap' feedback. Criteria uniformly met for all keys.
requirements.site_hook: New keyboard object (key size, pitch, travel, force, handwear); compare with Table VII

requirements.title: Slope of non-portable keyboards
requirements.text: The slope of non-portable keyboards shall be 0 to 25 degrees (0 to 15 degrees preferred) above the horizontal.
requirements.site_hook: Keyboard/console surface tilt parameter in sandbox; compare to 0-25 deg (0-15 preferred)

requirements.title: Multiple keyboards same configuration
requirements.text: Systems with more than one keyboard shall keep the same configuration of alphanumeric, numeric and special function keys.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Keyboard tactile feedback
requirements.text: Tactile feedback shall be provided (e.g., spring-loaded keys that click and return).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Keyboard lighting
requirements.text: Keyboards used in darkened environments shall have lighted keys dimmable to a minimum of 30 incremental positions from full ON to OFF; indicator lights dim concurrently; characters backlit; low-level white light per SAE AS25050.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Mouse orientation accuracy
requirements.text: User shall be able to orient the mouse within 10 degrees of correct orientation without visual reference (cursor moving between 350 and 10 degrees for straight up y movement); smooth cursor movement in same direction +/-10 degrees (5.1.3.3.2.3).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Mouse handedness
requirements.text: The mouse shall be operable with either the left or right hand; shaped for grasp by either hand in relaxed neutral posture with minimal wrist deviation, flexion or extension (5.1.3.3.5).
requirements.site_hook: Mouse/handheld object; wrist deviation from posture analysis when hand placed on mouse

requirements.title: Mouse buttons
requirements.text: Mouse buttons operable without diminishing control; finger actuates from neutral posture; contact surfaces perpendicular to displacement direction (5.1.3.3.4.1-3). Cable long enough for slack (5.1.3.3.3).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Mouse dimensions and button characteristics
requirements.text: Mouse width 40-70 mm (1.6-2.8 in); length 70-120 mm (2.8-4.7 in); height 25-40 mm (1-1.6 in); button resistance 0.5-1.5 N (1.8-5.4 oz); button displacement 5-6 mm (0.20-0.24 in).
requirements.site_hook: Mouse object (W, L, H); compare to Table VIII; optionally compare with mannequin hand length/breadth

requirements.title: Trackball general
requirements.text: Trackballs used only as position controls; off-edge indicators; buttons located to prevent accidental actuation; finger-controlled trackball primary button near thumb; no cross-coupling or backlash; control ratios for gross and fine positioning (5.1.3.4.1-5.1.3.4.5.3).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Trackball limb support
requirements.text: When trackballs are used for precise or continuous adjustments, wrist support or arm support, or both, shall be provided.
requirements.site_hook: Check console surface under forearm/wrist in operating posture

requirements.title: Trackball dimensions, resistance and clearances
requirements.text: D diameter min 50 mm (2 in), preferred 100 mm (4 in), max 150 mm (6 in); A surface exposure min 100°, preferred 120°, max 140°; resistance (precision required) min 0.25 N (0.9 oz), preferred 0.3 N (1.1 oz), max 1.5 N (5.4 oz); max 1.7 N (6 oz) in vibration or acceleration conditions; initial resistance 0.25 N (0.9 oz) to 0.4 N (1.4 oz). Clearances: S display centerline to ball centerline min 0, max 320 mm (12.6 in); C around ball min 50 mm (2 in); F ball to shelf front min 120 mm (4.75 in), max 250 mm (10 in). Permanent mounting as shown (5.1.3.4.7.2); smaller diameters acceptable where no precision needed (5.1.3.4.7.1).

values.quantity: display CL to ball CL lateral offset S

requirements.site_hook: Trackball object on console: compute lateral offset from display centerline and distance to console front edge; compare

requirements.title: Displacement joystick general
requirements.text: Displacement joysticks preferred when accuracy more critical than speed; spring-loaded return to center for rate control; off-edge indicators; deadband restrictions with automatic sequencing (5.1.3.5.1.1-6).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Joystick buttons
requirements.text: Buttons on hand-operated joysticks operable with a normal grip without diminishing control; located to prevent accidental actuation (not where the heel of hand rests); coded by shape, size, location, texture (5.1.3.5.2.4); trigger guards (5.1.3.5.2.3).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Hand-operated joystick movement limit
requirements.text: Movement of a hand-operated joystick shall not exceed 45 degrees from the center position; smooth in all directions; delay between control movement and display response not greater than 0.1 second (5.1.3.5.2.2.6).
requirements.site_hook: Joystick object with max deflection; compute wrist ROM required at full deflection

requirements.title: Displacement joystick dimensions, resistance and clearance
requirements.text: D diameter 6.5 mm (0.25 in) min to 16 mm (0.625 in) max; L length 75 mm (3 in) to 150 mm (6 in); resistance 3.3 N (12 oz) to 8.9 N (32 oz); A displacement max 45° (785 mrad); S display centerline to stick centerline 0 to 400 mm (15.75 in); C clearance around stick min = maximum stick excursion plus 100 mm (4 in); F stick centerline to shelf front 120 mm (4.75 in) to 250 mm (10 in). Recessed mounting may be used for finger-operated joysticks for precision.

values.quantity: display CL to stick CL S
stick CL to shelf front F

requirements.site_hook: Joystick object on console; compute lateral offset to display centerline, distance to console front, clearance to neighbouring objects

requirements.title: Joystick hand grip length
requirements.text: The hand grip length shall be 110 to 180 mm (4.3 to 7.1 in).
requirements.site_hook: Joystick grip object length; can compare to mannequin hand breadth (P95 male)
requirements.percentile_rule: grip length should accommodate P95 hand breadth (inferred)

requirements.title: Joystick hand grip diameter
requirements.text: The hand grip diameter shall be not more than 50 mm (2 in).
requirements.site_hook: Grip object diameter vs max; compare to P5 female grip diameter

requirements.title: Joystick hand clearance
requirements.text: Clearances of 100 mm (4 in) to the side and 50 mm (2 in) to the rear shall be provided to allow for hand movement; clearance for full range of motion and button actuation in any position (5.1.3.5.2.5.4-5).
requirements.site_hook: Clearance measurement from joystick grip to nearest sandbox object laterally and rearward; or sweep mannequin hand through joystick range and check collisions

requirements.title: Joystick forearm/wrist support
requirements.text: Joysticks shall be mounted to provide forearm or wrist support; modular devices mounted to allow actuation without slippage, movement or tilting of base (5.1.3.5.2.5.7). Same for finger-operated (5.1.3.5.3.3) and thumbtip/fingertip (hand or wrist support, 5.1.3.5.4.4).
requirements.site_hook: Check armrest/console under forearm in operating posture

requirements.title: Thumbtip/fingertip joystick movement
requirements.text: Thumbtip- or fingertip-operated displacement joystick movement shall not exceed 45 degrees from center; grip shall not simultaneously function as a joystick (5.1.3.5.4.1).
requirements.site_hook: Joystick object parameter

requirements.title: Isometric hand joystick maximum force
requirements.text: Maximum force for full output of hand-operated isometric joysticks shall be not more than 118 newtons (26.7 lbs). Dimensions, resistance and clearance per 5.1.3.5.2.5.
requirements.site_hook: User enters force; compare and also compare to P5 female strength

requirements.title: Isometric joystick use
requirements.text: Isometric joysticks selected when speed more critical than accuracy; avoid where constant force held for long periods; off-edge indicators; button placement; coding (5.1.3.6.1.2-5.1.3.6.2.5).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Grid-and-stylus devices
requirements.text: Cursor at stylus coordinates; click feedback; zero-order control only; smooth movement; overlay grids conform to display size; displaced grids approximate display size and are mounted below display preserving directional relationships (5.1.3.7.1-5.1.3.7.3.2).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item; grid mounting below display could be geometric

requirements.title: Stylus force on tablet
requirements.text: Stylus force required to produce continuous input on a tablet shall be not greater than 0.8 newtons (2.9 ozf).
requirements.site_hook: User parameter

requirements.title: Light pen dimensions and weight
requirements.text: Light pen shall be 120 to 180 mm (4.7 to 7.1 in) long with a diameter of 7 to 20 mm (0.3 to 0.8 in); slip-resistant surface; weigh 0.1 to 0.25 newtons (0.35 to 0.875 ozf) (5.1.3.8.3.2); stowage provided (5.1.3.8.3.3).
requirements.site_hook: Tool/handheld object dimensions and mass

requirements.title: Stylus/light pen buttons
requirements.text: Contact surface of a selector button on a stylus or light pen shall have diameter not less than 0.05 mm (0.2 in) [as printed; 0.2 in = 5 mm]; force to actuate 0.3 to 0.8 newton (1 to 2.9 ozf).

requirements.site_hook: User parameter

requirements.title: Pucks
requirements.text: Use and characteristics of pucks shall be in accordance with ISO 9241-400.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Hand-held free-moving x-y-z controllers
requirements.text: Relative positional reference in roll/pitch/yaw, at least one push button, defined operating space; loss of reference alerts user and inputs ignored.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Data entry, cursors, function keys, light pen entry (summary)
requirements.text: 5.1.3.11.1-5.1.3.11.9: user-paced entry, positive feedback, explicit ENTER and DELETE, validation, abbreviations, cursor control and movement relationships, keyboard data entry (numeric keypad for substantial numeric input), fixed and variable function keys, light pen feedback, directional controllers with discrete actuate/deactuate mechanism. Software/dialog items, summarized only.
requirements.site_hook: Out of scope (software dialog)

requirements.title: Interactive control dialogs (summary)
requirements.text: 5.1.3.12.1-5.1.3.12.8.3: control action simplicity, lockout, hierarchical levels (no more than four; menus no more than three levels should be used), menus, form filling, command language, question-and-answer, query language, graphic/iconic interaction. Software/dialog items, summarized only.
requirements.site_hook: Out of scope (software dialog)

requirements.title: Rotary selector switch use
requirements.text: Rotary selector switches should be used for discrete functions when three or more detented positions are required; not for two-position functions unless prompt visual identification is primary and speed not critical.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Rotary selector pointer and shape
requirements.text: Moving pointer and fixed scale; bar-shaped knob with parallel sides tapered to a point (should); shape coding when different-function rotary controls on same panel may be confused (5.1.4.1.1.1.3.2).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Discrete rotary selector switch dimensions, resistance, displacement, separation
requirements.text: L length 25 mm (1 in) min, 100 mm (4 in) max; W width max 25 mm (1 in); H depth 16 mm (0.625 in) min, 75 mm (3 in) max; resistance 115 mN·m (1 in-lbf) min, 680 mN·m (6 in-lbf) max. A displacement between detents: 15° (262 mrad) min to 40° (700 mrad) max for facilitating performance; 30° (525 mrad) min to 90° (1,570 mrad) max when special engineering requirements demand large separation or tactually ('blind') positioned controls. Separation between adjacent edges of areas swept: one-hand random min 25 mm (1 in), preferred 50 mm (2 in); two-handed operation min 75 mm (3 in), preferred 125 mm (5 in).
requirements.site_hook: Rotary selector control object (L, W, H, detent angle, torque); separation measured between swept circles of adjacent knobs

requirements.title: Rotary selector number of positions
requirements.text: A rotary selector switch not visible during normal operation shall have no more than 12 positions; constantly visible switch not more than 24 positions; positions not opposite each other unless knob shape precludes confusion; elastic snap resistance.
requirements.site_hook: Control parameter: number of positions + visibility (could use line-of-sight check for visibility)

requirements.title: Rotary switch reference line contrast
requirements.text: A reference line shall be provided; luminance contrast ratio not less than 3:1 under all lighting conditions.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Rotary switch parallax error
requirements.text: Pointer mounted close to scale; from the normal user's position, parallax errors shall not exceed 25 percent of the distance between scale markings.

requirements.title: Knob attachment
requirements.text: Shafts and knobs designed only for intended orientation; attachment precludes slipping and reversed replacement.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Key-operated switch (single function) dimensions
requirements.text: A displacement 30° (525 mrad) min to 90° (1,570 mrad) max; H height 13 mm (0.5 in) min to 75 mm (3 in) max; resistance 115 mN·m (1 in-lbf) min to 680 mN·m (6 in-lbf) max.
requirements.site_hook: Key switch object parameters

requirements.title: KOS coding
requirements.text: Red reserved for emergency functions; shape coding avoids sharp corners; size coding no more than two sizes within figure 7 height limits.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Multifunction KOS geometry
requirements.text: OFF position of multifunction KOSs shall be located at 300 degrees; total angular displacement not greater than 120 degrees (5.1.4.1.1.2.6); key vertical = OFF (5.1.4.1.1.2.9); actuation clockwise from vertical OFF (5.1.4.1.1.2.11); key removable only when OFF; single-row teeth up or forward.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Key lock systems (vehicle)
requirements.text: Vehicle exterior door locks prevent lock-out; weatherproof; single key for multiple locks; distinct locks for limited access; auditory signal for key left in ignition (5.1.4.1.1.2.12-16).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Discrete thumbwheel design

requirements.title: Thumbwheel digit visibility angle
requirements.text: Thumbwheels shall not preclude viewing the digits within a 30-degree viewing angle to the left and right of a line perpendicular to the thumbwheel digits; readout viewable from all user positions (5.1.4.1.1.3.9).

requirements.title: Knob dimensions, torque, separation

Beyond 480 mm (19 in) two-hand operation becomes less effective.

values.quantity: force factor in front of opposite arm
two-hand effective zone forward of NSRP

requirements.title: Lever location compatible with reach and strength

requirements.site_hook: Reach check to lever at full travel extremes; joint angles/RULA at extremes
