requirements.site_hook: Distance from mannequin headset/chest point (seated working posture) to control box object; also hand reach check

requirements.title: Label characteristics consistent with reading distance and conditions
requirements.text: Label characteristics shall be consistent with requirements for accuracy of identification, time available for recognition or other responses, distance at which the labels must be read, illumination level and color, criticality of the function labeled, and label design within and among controls and systems.
requirements.site_hook: Label object carries reading distance (measured from mannequin eye), illumination and criticality; feeds Tables XVIII/XIX

requirements.title: Controls and displays clearly labeled
requirements.text: Controls and displays shall be appropriately and clearly labeled with the basic information needed for proper identification, utilization, actuation, or manipulation of the item. Labels shall be provided whenever necessary to locate and identify items, follow procedures, or avoid hazards (5.4.1.3). Control labels shall indicate the functional result of control movement (5.4.1.5).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist: every sandbox control/display has a label object

requirements.title: Hierarchical labeling scheme
requirements.text: A hierarchical labeling scheme shall be used on panels: major labels for major systems/workstations, group labels for subsystems/functional groups, component labels for each element; do not repeat higher-level information in lower-level labels. Labels shall be graduated in size (5.4.1.7.1).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist; label objects could carry a hierarchy level

requirements.title: Group label characters larger than control/display labels
requirements.text: The characters in group labels shall be larger than those used to identify individual controls and displays, unless analysis shows that individual control labels should have primacy. The characters identifying controls and displays shall be larger than the characters identifying control positions (5.4.1.7.1.2).
requirements.site_hook: Compare character heights of label objects by hierarchy level

requirements.title: Size step between label levels
requirements.text: With the smallest characters determined by viewing conditions, the dimensions (height and width) of each character shall be at least 25 percent larger than those of the next smaller label.

values.quantity: character height and width step to next smaller label level

requirements.site_hook: Label objects with hierarchy level; check each level >= 1.25 x the next lower level

requirements.title: Letter size in hierarchical labels (Figure 30)
requirements.text: Labels should be graduated in letter size such that system or workstation labels are about 25 percent larger than subsystem or functional group labels, subsystem or functional group labels are about 25 percent larger than component labels, and component labels are about 25 percent larger than control position labels (see figure 30). Figure 30 shows five levels: equipment title (largest), panel title (second largest), subpanel title (third largest), function/component label (fourth largest), control position labels (smallest).

values.quantity: size ratio between successive label levels

requirements.site_hook: Given the smallest (control-position) character height from Table XVIII, report recommended heights x1.25, x1.56, x1.95, x2.44 for higher levels

requirements.title: Lines of demarcation contrast
requirements.text: Lines of demarcation shall have enough contrast to be visually distinctive from the panel background.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Consistent label location
requirements.text: Labels shall be consistently located relative to the object being labeled throughout the system.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Labels readable regardless of control position
requirements.text: Control labels shall be located so that they are readable regardless of the position of the control; labels shall be visible to the user during control actuation (5.4.2.2.1); all discrete functional control positions shall be identified (5.4.2.2.2); direction of motion should be identified for continuous rotary controls (5.4.2.2.3).
requirements.site_hook: With the mannequin hand on the control (reach posture), ray-cast from eye to label and test occlusion by the hand/arm

requirements.title: Labels not obscured
requirements.text: Labels shall not obscure, or be obscured, by other sources of information.
requirements.site_hook: Line-of-sight occlusion test from eye point to label

requirements.title: Label on or near the item
requirements.text: Labels shall be placed on or very near the items that they identify.
requirements.site_hook: Distance from label object to its control/display object; flag if label closer to another control

requirements.title: Label above controls at or below eye level
requirements.text: When controls are placed at or below eye level, the corresponding label should be placed above the controls or display that they describe. When controls are above eye level, the label may be located below the control if label visibility will be enhanced (5.4.3.2).
requirements.site_hook: Compare control height with the mannequin eye height in the working posture; check label Z > control Z when control is at/below eye level
requirements.percentile_rule: use eye height of the operator percentile range

requirements.title: Labels not near the floor
requirements.text: Labels shall not be placed near the floor or other positions that preclude the observer from easily viewing the label from work posture appropriate to the equipment.
requirements.site_hook: Check label lies within the visual field (e.g. within the comfortable downward gaze/head-tilt range) from the work posture; flag labels below knee height without a kneeling/squatting work posture

requirements.title: Overhead panel labels upright from operating position
requirements.text: On overhead panels, markings and labeling should be oriented so that they appear upright when viewed from the user's operational position. Overhead items out of view should be identified with labels on walls with an arrow pointing to the item (5.4.3.5).
requirements.site_hook: Label orientation vector vs the mannequin's head up-vector when looking at the overhead panel

requirements.title: No labels on movable controls that rotate upside down
requirements.text: Labels shall not be placed on movable controls that allow the label to rotate to an upside-down position. Pictorial symbols shall not be used on a control that may rotate and position the symbol so that it may be confusing (5.4.9.3).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Redundant labeling for multi-plane items
requirements.text: Redundant labeling shall be used for installations such as pipes that take several runs and can be viewed from several planes or components that can be viewed from two sides.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Adjacent labels separated
requirements.text: Adjacent labels shall be sufficiently separated to not be read as one continuous label.
requirements.site_hook: Gap between adjacent label objects compared with word spacing (>= 3/5 char height, 5.4.7.9) and clearance (>= 1/2 char height, 5.4.7.13.2)

requirements.title: Group label placement
requirements.text: Labels shall identify functionally grouped controls (5.4.3.9). When a line encloses a functional group, the label shall be centered at the top of the group in a break in the line or just below the line; in colored areas, centered at the top within the area (5.4.3.9.2); if insufficient room, in the best available space provided the grouping is demarcated (5.4.3.9.3).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Label orientation (Figure 31)
requirements.text: The orientation of labels shall conform to figure 31: primary = horizontal, read left to right (5.4.4.1); secondary = vertical, letters upright and stacked, reading top to bottom (5.4.4.2.2, 5.4.4.2.3); text rotated 90 degrees in either direction is unacceptable, and stacked letters reading bottom to top is unacceptable. Vertical orientation should be used only when labels are not critical for safety or performance and where space is limited (5.4.4.2.1).
requirements.site_hook: Label object orientation enum: horizontal / vertical-stacked; rotated text flagged

requirements.title: Labels legible at operational reading distance
requirements.text: Labels shall be easy to read accurately from the operational reading distances and in the anticipated vibration and illumination environments. Design shall consider contrast, height, width, stroke width, spacing, style, method of application, wording and specular reflection (5.4.5.2).
requirements.site_hook: Measure eye-to-label distance for the farthest user (e.g. P5 seated back / P95 standing) and apply 5.4.7.1/Table XVIII/Table XIX

requirements.title: Labels on outside of covers and access openings
requirements.text: Labels shall be placed on the outside of equipment covers to identify control, display, or other functions located within a covered compartment. Access openings shall be labeled to identify the functions of items accessible through them (5.4.5.4).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist; hatch/access-opening objects could have a label flag

requirements.title: Cable labels visible to maintainer
requirements.text: Labels attached to lines or cables shall be positioned so the label is visible and properly oriented with respect to the normal viewing position of the maintainer. Both ends of a cable shall be labeled (5.4.5.5.1); connection elements shall have matching labels (5.4.5.5.2).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Label color for maximum contrast
requirements.text: Label color(s) shall be chosen for maximum contrast against the label background and surrounding equipment. Labels with independent backgrounds shall provide contrast between lettering and background (5.4.5.6.5). Shiny metallic backgrounds shall not be used (5.4.5.6.6).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Dark-on-light above 10 lx
requirements.text: When the ambient illumination will be above 10 lx (0.9 fc), dark characters on a light background should be used. When dark adaptation is required, markings should be white on a dark background (5.4.5.6.4).

values.quantity: ambient illuminance threshold for dark-on-light labels

requirements.site_hook: Label polarity vs user-entered ambient illuminance

requirements.title: Number of label colors
requirements.text: If color coding is used, the number of different colors shall not exceed five.
requirements.site_hook: Count distinct label colors in the scene

requirements.title: Same words not for non-identical functions
requirements.text: The same words shall not be used to identify two or more controls or displays when they are not functionally identical. Labels shall be consistent within and across panels (5.4.6.8). Trade names and irrelevant information shall not appear on labels (5.4.6.13).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item (could auto-detect duplicate label text in the sandbox)

requirements.title: Character height by visual angle
requirements.text: Character height should subtend a visual angle of 4.4 milliradians (15 minutes) (viewing distance multiplied by 0.004) as a minimum; a visual angle of 5.8 milliradians (20 minutes) (viewing distance multiplied by 0.006) is preferred.

values.condition: as printed; note 4.4 mrad = 0.0044 and 5.8 mrad = 0.0058

requirements.site_hook: Minimum label height = eye-to-label distance x 0.004 (preferred x 0.006); use the farthest anticipated viewer
requirements.percentile_rule: farthest viewer (largest eye-to-label distance across postures/percentiles)

requirements.title: Legibility at 710 mm
requirements.text: Unless circumstances require otherwise, labels shall be clearly legible at a viewing distance of 710 mm (28 in). The recommended height for letters and numerals at this distance is approximately 5 mm (0.18 in). Table XVIII gives minimum character heights for other viewing distances.
requirements.site_hook: Default label reading distance 710 mm when no measured distance is available

requirements.title: Minimum character height vs viewing distance
requirements.text: Minimum character height: viewing distance less than 0.5 m (20 in): 2.3 mm (0.1 in); 0.5 to 1.0 m (20 to 40 in): 4.7 mm (0.2 in); 1.0 to 2.0 m (40 to 80 in): 9.4 mm (0.4 in); 2.0 to 4.0 m (80 to 160 in): 18 mm (0.75 in); 4.0 to 9.0 m (160 to 360 in): 38 mm (1.5 in). Label size on cabinets shall be consistent with viewing distance per table XVIII (5.4.10.2.4).

values.condition: viewing distance 0.5 to 1.0 m (20 to 40 in)
viewing distance 1.0 to 2.0 m (40 to 80 in)
viewing distance 2.0 to 4.0 m (80 to 160 in)
viewing distance 4.0 to 9.0 m (160 to 360 in)

requirements.site_hook: Lookup by measured eye-to-label distance; compare to label object character height

requirements.title: Minimum character height vs luminance
requirements.text: Labels shall be clearly visible under all conditions of expected luminance (5.4.7.3). Table XIX minimum character heights (at 710 mm): critical markings with variable position (e.g., numerals on counters): 5 mm (0.2 in) at 3.5 cd/m² (1 fL) or below, 3 mm (0.12 in) above 3.5 cd/m²; critical markings with fixed position (e.g., numerals on fixed scales, controls, emergency instructions): 4 mm (0.16 in) / 2.5 mm (0.1 in); non-critical markings (e.g., identification labels, routine instructions): 2.5 mm (0.1 in) / 2.5 mm (0.1 in). NOTE: values assume a 710 mm (28 in) viewing distance; for other distances multiply by D/710 mm (D/28 in).

values.condition: luminance <= 3.5 cd/m2 (1 fL); scale by D/710 mm
luminance > 3.5 cd/m2; scale by D/710 mm
luminance <= 3.5 cd/m2; scale by D/710 mm
luminance > 3.5 cd/m2; scale by D/710 mm
any luminance; scale by D/710 mm

requirements.site_hook: Label object: criticality + luminance class; required height = table value x (measured eye distance / 710 mm)

requirements.title: Stroke width, normal illumination (dark on light)
requirements.text: If labels are expected to be read under normal illumination and black characters are specified on a white or light background, the stroke width should be 1/6 to 1/7 of the height.
requirements.site_hook: Label object stroke-width parameter

requirements.title: Stroke width, dim illumination (light on dark)
requirements.text: Where dark adaptation is required or legibility at night is a critical factor and white characters are specified on a dark background, the stroke width of the characters should be 1/7 to 1/8 of the height.
requirements.site_hook: Label object stroke-width parameter

requirements.title: Stroke width, transilluminated characters
requirements.text: For transilluminated characters, the stroke width should be 1/10 of the height.
requirements.site_hook: Label object stroke-width parameter

requirements.title: Consistent stroke width
requirements.text: The stroke width shall be the same for all letters and numerals of equal height. The stroke width ratios apply regardless of character height for distance viewing; where different stroke widths are used on one sign for emphasis, the thinnest stroke shall be no less than 1/8 nor the thickest stroke greater than 2/5 of the respective character heights (5.4.7.4.5).
requirements.site_hook: Label object stroke-width parameter

requirements.title: Character width-to-height ratio
requirements.text: The width-to-height ratio for numerals and letters should be 3:5. Exceptions: 'M' and 'W' 4:5; 'I' and '1' one stroke wide; '4' one stroke wider (5.4.7.5.2). Where wide characters are required (curved surfaces, column alignment), the ratio may be increased to as much as 1:1 (5.4.7.5.3).

values.condition: 3:5 nominal; M,W 4:5; up to 1:1 for wide characters

requirements.site_hook: Label object font metrics

requirements.title: Letter width
requirements.text: The width of letters should be 3/5 to 4/5 of the height, except for 'I', which should be 1/10 to 2/5 of the height.
requirements.site_hook: Label object font metrics

requirements.title: Numeral width
requirements.text: The width of numerals should be 3/5 of the height, except for '4', which should be 4/5 of the height, and '1', which should be 1/5 of the height.
requirements.site_hook: Label object font metrics

requirements.title: Stencil stroke breaks
requirements.text: Stencil characters shall not have stroke breaks greater than 1/2 the character stroke width. Continuous stroke characters should be used where practical (5.4.7.7.1).
requirements.site_hook: Label object parameter

requirements.title: Character spacing
requirements.text: The minimum space between characters shall be one stroke width.
requirements.site_hook: Label object spacing parameter

requirements.title: Word spacing
requirements.text: The minimum space between words shall not be less than 3/5 of the character height.
requirements.site_hook: Label object spacing parameter

requirements.title: Line spacing
requirements.text: The minimum space between lines shall be approximately one-half the character height (e.g., line spacing in points equals 1/2 the font size in points).
requirements.site_hook: Label object spacing parameter

requirements.title: Letter case on labels
requirements.text: Single-word or unitary-object labels (e.g., FEED PUMP) shall be all capital letters; phrases or sentences shall be mixed case (5.4.7.11.2); capitals should be used for abbreviations (5.4.7.11.3); capitals shall be used for identification labels, headings, signal words, legends and short message labels (5.4.7.11.4).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item (could auto-check label text case)

requirements.title: Plain sans-serif style
requirements.text: Letters and numerals shall be of a plain style using sans-serif fonts, except as necessary to distinguish confusable characters (L, I, 1, 0, O). For confusable pairs: lower case 'l' with a short bottom extension to the right; numeral '1' with a short top extension to the left; numeral '0' narrower than letter 'O' (5.4.7.12.2).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Minimum clearance around characters
requirements.text: There shall be a minimum clearance around a character or word of at least 1/2 the character height. There shall be clear space between characters and words to facilitate reading at the expected distances (5.4.7.13.1).
requirements.site_hook: Label object margin vs character height; also gap to neighbouring labels/edges

requirements.title: Label attachment
requirements.text: Labels not part of the equipment shall be securely attached (5.4.8.1), attached to a structural member not removed during servicing (5.4.8.2), removable without damaging the surface (5.4.8.5), and remain legible for the overhaul interval (5.4.8.14). Metallic labels mounted to prevent galvanic corrosion (5.4.8.4).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Labels on flat surfaces; curved labels
requirements.text: Whenever practicable, labels should be mounted on a flat surface; curved labels (wrapped around pipe or cable) should be avoided (5.4.8.7). If on a curved surface, lettering shall be completely visible from the normal viewing position (5.4.8.8). When curvature makes lettering too small to read, another mode of labeling such as an attached tag shall be used (5.4.8.10).
requirements.site_hook: For a label on a cylinder: angular span of text vs visible arc from the eye point

requirements.title: Non-reflective label materials
requirements.text: Labels shall be constructed of non-reflective materials to avoid illegibility due to a light source being reflected back to the user.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Tag hardware not interfering
requirements.text: The length of the attaching hardware should be minimized so that the tag does not interfere with the operation or maintenance of the equipment; tag hardware shall be durable (5.4.8.11).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Labels mounted to minimize wear and dirt
requirements.text: Labels shall be mounted to minimize wear or obscuration by grease, grime, or dirt. If grease, grime, or dirt are likely to accumulate, the labels should be mounted on a vertical surface.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist; label surface orientation (vertical) could be read from the sandbox

requirements.title: Temporary labels and tag-outs not obscuring labels
requirements.text: Temporary labels shall not obscure prior permanent labels unless replaced. Tag-outs shall clearly identify out-of-service items, be securely affixed, not obscure associated or adjacent labels/devices, and physically prevent actuation of a control (5.4.8.16.1-5.4.8.16.5).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Arrow shape (Figure 32)
requirements.text: Arrows used in labels or markings shall be clearly recognizable and easily identifiable from typical viewing distances. Simple forms with sharp angles and a tapered overall shape are preferable to wide angles and a relatively uniform overall shape (see figure 32).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Weight and CG placard over 13.6 kg
requirements.text: Weight and center of gravity placards shall be placed on any unit of equipment that must be moved for maintenance if its weight exceeds 13.6 kg (30 lb).
requirements.site_hook: Sandbox box/equipment mass: if > 13.6 kg, require a weight & CG label flag

requirements.title: Number of lifters label
requirements.text: If a unit of equipment is designed to be lifted or carried by more than one person, the label shall include the number of people recommended to lift or carry it.
requirements.site_hook: Use the lifting module (mass vs one-person lift limit) to recommend the number of lifters and require it on the label

requirements.title: Unobstructed unit/part identification label
requirements.text: Each unit, assembly, subassembly, and part shall contain a label placed in a location that provides no visual obstruction from the defined user's viewing area. The gross identifying label shall be located externally, not obscured by adjacent items, on the flattest most uncluttered surface or main chassis (5.4.10.1.3).
requirements.site_hook: Occlusion ray-cast from the maintainer's eye position to the label

requirements.title: Panel and subfunction labels
requirements.text: Each panel shall be labeled if it must be identified from others; a system/subsystem label where a panel integrates a distinct function (5.4.10.1.6); subfunction areas shall have a label approximately centered above the area (5.4.10.1.7); non-uniform subfunction areas should have a border (5.4.10.1.8).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Cabinet labels
requirements.text: When several equipment cabinets are in one work area, each cabinet shall be labeled to identify its contents; cabinet identification labels shall be in a conspicuous position with respect to typical observation points (5.4.10.2.2); storage cabinet contents labeled on the outside of the door (5.4.10.2.3.1); a redundant contents label visible when the door is open (5.4.10.2.3.3).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Cabinet label at standing eye height
requirements.text: For large storage cabinets, labels should be placed at standing eye height (i.e., between 127 to 165 cm [50 to 65 in] above the standing surface).
requirements.site_hook: Label object Z height on cabinet; also compare to standing eye height of P5 female to P95 male from the selected survey
requirements.percentile_rule: standing eye height range of the user population

requirements.title: Label differentiation by character height
requirements.text: Labels for identifying prime equipment cabinets, panels, subfunctions on a panel, and individual panel components shall be capable of being differentiated in terms of the label character height (see 5.4.1.7).
requirements.site_hook: Same as 5.4.1.7.1.3 (>= 25% step per level)

requirements.title: Instruction plates and diagrams
requirements.text: Instruction plates shall be as brief as clarity allows and placed where the user can easily see them; instructions read left to right in step-by-step format (5.4.10.3.5); diagrams oriented to relate directly to the objects (5.4.10.3.7) and located in conspicuous places on or near controls (5.4.10.3.8).
requirements.site_hook: Visibility check from the operator eye point to the instruction plate

requirements.title: Lift and hoist point marking
requirements.text: Lift and hoist points shall be clearly marked indicating weight and stress limitations, and labeled at the point of lift, not on removable parts (5.4.10.4.2).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Prominent warning labels
requirements.text: If hazards to personnel or equipment may be present, appropriate warning signs or labels shall be displayed prominently, in accordance with appropriate safety standards (5.4.10.5.2). Also see 5.7.2.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Accommodate target audience with clothing and gear
requirements.text: The design shall accommodate the target audience population that will interact with the system or facility and the clothing and gear the target population will be wearing, carrying, and stowing on the system as specified (see 6.2). The system design shall allow operation, maintenance, and support in all environmental conditions and extremes as specified (5.5.1.2).
requirements.site_hook: Mannequin population/percentile selector plus clothing/gear allowances (e.g. arctic clothing, body armor, CBRNE) applied to clearances and reach
requirements.percentile_rule: full specified target population including clothing and gear

requirements.title: Manned space definition
requirements.text: Indoor climate requirements shall be provided for 'manned spaces'. A space is considered 'manned' if it is designed for manned entry and routinely occupied continuously for more than a short interval, which typically means 20 minutes. Spaces not requiring HVAC shall be specified (5.5.2.1).

values.quantity: continuous occupancy defining a manned space

requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Thermostat per manned location
requirements.text: Each manned location (area connected by a common ventilation system) shall have its own thermostat for temperature regulation and dehumidification.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Minimum interior heating temperature
requirements.text: Within work environments occupied during extended periods of time including mobile personnel enclosures, heating shall be provided to maintain interior dry bulb temperature above 10 °C (50 °F).
requirements.site_hook: Environment panel: user enters design temperature

requirements.title: Hand warmth for precise work below 16 °C
requirements.text: If precise work is done for more than 20 minutes in an environment below 16 °C (60 °F), special provisions should be made to keep hands warm. Heated air discharge shall not be directed on personnel (5.5.2.1.2.2).
requirements.site_hook: Environment panel

requirements.title: Total ventilation air, small enclosures
requirements.text: For enclosures less than 4.25 m³ per person, a minimum of 0.85 m³ (30 ft³) of total ventilation air per minute per person shall be introduced into the enclosure; outside fresh air shall be supplied at a minimum rate of 0.57 m³/min (20 ft³/min) per person (5.5.2.1.3.2.1). The number of people is specified by the procuring activity.
requirements.site_hook: Compute enclosure volume per occupant from a cabin/room object and number of mannequins; user enters airflow

requirements.title: Air exchanges, larger enclosures
requirements.text: For enclosures larger than 4.25 m³ per person, outside fresh air shall be supplied at a rate sufficient to produce at least six complete air exchanges per hour.
requirements.site_hook: Room volume x 6 per hour -> required fresh air flow

requirements.title: Maximum air velocity
requirements.text: Air velocities shall not exceed 30 m/min (100 ft/min) (0.5 m/s or 1.7 ft/s) at any measured position in the space. Exception: where spot cooling of personnel is provided, not more than 60 m/min (200 ft/min) (5.5.2.1.3.4.2). Where manuals or loose papers are used, not more than 20 m/min (65 ft/min) (5.5.2.1.3.4.3).
requirements.site_hook: Environment panel

requirements.title: Ventilation for harmful substances
requirements.text: Ventilation or other protective measures shall keep gases, vapors, dust, and fumes within the permissible exposure limits of 29 CFR 1910, ACGIH TLVs, or DoDI 6055.01; intakes located to minimize contaminated air (5.5.2.1.3.7).
requirements.site_hook: External limits; not a geometry check

requirements.title: Relative humidity and temperature design goal
requirements.text: The HVAC system shall be capable of providing and maintaining a relative humidity within a range from 30 percent minimum to 70 percent maximum with 40 percent to 45 percent preferred. The temperature/humidity design goal shall be between 21 °C and 25 °C (70 °F and 77 °F) and 45 percent humidity. Cold air shall not be directly discharged on personnel unless it can be redirected (5.5.2.1.4.1).
requirements.site_hook: Environment panel

requirements.title: Temperature uniformity floor-to-head
requirements.text: The temperature of the air at floor level and at head level at any personnel position shall not differ by more than 5.5 °C (10 °F); less than 3.0 °C (5 °F) is preferred. Side wall temperature differences of 11 °C (20 °F) or less do not significantly degrade comfort. In berthing areas, the difference between the inside bulkhead/wall surface adjacent to the berthing and the average air temperature shall be less than 10 °C (18 °F).

values.quantity: berthing wall surface vs average air temperature

requirements.site_hook: Head level can be taken from the mannequin (seated/standing head height); user enters temperatures

requirements.title: Micro-climate with protective clothing
requirements.text: When special protective clothing or personal equipment (pressure suits, fuel handler suits, body armor, arctic clothing, temperature regulated clothing) are worn, a comfort micro-climate between 20 °C (68 °F), 14 mm Hg (0.55 in Hg) ambient water vapor pressure and 35 °C (95 °F), 3 mm Hg (0.12 in Hg) ambient water vapor pressure is desirable and, where possible, shall be maintained by heat transfer systems.

values.condition: 20 degC at 14 mm Hg to 35 degC at 3 mm Hg vapor pressure

requirements.site_hook: Environment panel

requirements.title: Maximum WBGTeff in manned spaces
requirements.text: The WBGTeff within manned spaces shall be no greater than 30 °C (86 °F) under normal operational internal heat loads and worst-case design climatic conditions (AR 70-38). Shipboard: apply PHELs (NEHC-TM-OEM 6260.6) if not met; aircraft cockpits: FITS (AFI 48-151); prolonged work above 250 watts metabolic rate: ACGIH TLV for WBGTeff.

values.quantity: metabolic rate above which ACGIH TLV applies

requirements.site_hook: WBGT calculator in an environment panel (inputs Tnwb, Tg, Tdb, clothing)

requirements.title: WBGT calculation
requirements.text: WBGTin = 0.7 Tnwb + 0.3 Tg (no direct sunlight); WBGTout = 0.7 Tnwb + 0.2 Tg + 0.1 Tdb (direct sunlight); WBGTeff = WBGTin/out + CAF (clothing-adjustment factor, table XX) (5.5.2.1.4.7.2).
requirements.site_hook: Implement formula in the environment panel

requirements.title: Clothing-adjustment factors for WBGT
requirements.text: CAF, °C (°F): long sleeve shirt & pants 0 (0); woven cloth coveralls 3.5 (6.3); double cloth coveralls 5.0 (9.0); turnout gear or ground crew ensemble 5.6 (10.0); body armor, humid conditions - add 2.8 (5.0); plastic coveralls over underwear 0.5 (0.9); hood with plastic coveralls - add 1.0 (1.8); MOPP4, easy work 5.6 (10.0); MOPP4, moderate or hard work 11.1 (20.0).

values.quantity: CAF turnout gear / ground crew ensemble

requirements.site_hook: Clothing selector shared with mannequin clothing allowances

requirements.title: Identify and mitigate adverse climate effects
requirements.text: Where the system will be exposed to precipitation, direct sunlight (solar loading), dust or other climatic effects during operation and maintenance, the designer shall identify all adverse effects upon personnel and equipment, and the design shall mitigate them (5.5.2.2.4).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item

requirements.title: Maintenance area air conditioning and heating thresholds
requirements.text: Air conditioning shall be provided, when feasible, if temperatures exceed 29.5 °C (85 °F) (5.5.2.2.5.1). Air heating shall be provided for shirt-sleeve maintenance where temperature will drop below 18 °C (64 °F) (5.5.2.2.5.9). Ventilation shall be provided in equipment trailers where personnel perform maintenance (5.5.2.2.5.2).

values.quantity: temperature above which AC provided (maintenance areas)
temperature below which heating provided (shirt-sleeve maintenance)

requirements.site_hook: Environment panel

requirements.title: Design for gloves/protective equipment in cold
requirements.text: Under extremely cold conditions or where there is significant wind-chill (below -12 °C [10 °F]), design for operations and maintenance shall accommodate the requirement for special gloves or other protective equipment.
requirements.site_hook: When cold condition is selected, apply arctic-mitten hand dimensions/clearances to controls, handles and access openings

requirements.title: Organizational maintenance without shelter at -29 °C
requirements.text: Maintenance shall be able to be performed without shelter at the organizational level when the temperature is as low as -29 °C (-20 °F) or an equivalent wind chill exists; equipment shall be designed (quick-disconnect servicing equipment) to require a minimum sustained working time. Heated working areas shall be provided above organizational level (5.5.2.2.5.7).

values.quantity: lowest temperature for unsheltered organizational maintenance

requirements.title: Fall-protection anchors on luminaire stanchions
requirements.text: Stanchions or poles supporting luminaires at the edge of ships or structures shall have anchor points on each side so a person wearing a safety harness can be secured to at least one anchor point at all times when climbing to and from the luminaire (see 4.9.3).

requirements.title: Portable and emergency lighting
requirements.text: Portable lighting shall be provided where fixed illumination is not provided. Emergency lighting shall be provided, automatically engage on failure (5.5.3.9.1), have an independent source (5.5.3.9.2), illuminate egress paths (5.5.3.9.4), and be located per NFPA 101 (5.5.3.9.5).

requirements.title: Illuminance ratio task vs surround

requirements.title: Hazardous noise evaluation threshold
requirements.text: Environments and conditions in which SPLs equal or exceed 85 dBA and 140 dBP even on an intermittent basis shall be evaluated in accordance with MIL-STD-1474 and the hearing conservation policy of the procuring activity. Controls, displays and monitoring workstations should be in acoustically isolated spaces (5.5.4.4.2).

requirements.title: Compatibility with hearing protection
requirements.text: The system shall be compatible with personal hearing protection worn within the context of mission performance; if authorized, the design shall accommodate wearing personal hearing protection devices. Hearing protectors shall reduce noise at the ear to a non-hazardous level (5.5.4.4.3.2).

requirements.title: Permissible noise exposure limits
requirements.text: Maximum permissible daily and occasional noise exposure shall not exceed figure 34 (5.5.4.4.4). Notes: Zone A, even with hearing protection no exposure to levels exceeding 120 dBA or a 24-hour Leq(24) exceeding 105 dBA. Zone B (occasional): both earmuffs and ear plugs; if exposure < 10 minutes either is sufficient. Zone C (occasional): earmuffs or plugs required. Zone D (daily): hearing protection worn. Zone E (no protection): for exposures of less than 8 hours, no exposure above 84 dBA; when remaining more than 8 hours in high-noise spaces, Leq(24) of 80 dBA shall not be exceeded; for at least a third of each 24 hours, environment not exceeding 75 dBA. Graph (read from figure, approximate): upper limit 120 dBA from 10 min to 1 hr, falling to about 110 dBA at 8 hr and to the Leq(24) = 105 line beyond; zone B between about 110 and 120 dBA; zone D up to about 110 dBA for up to 8 hr (about 100-110 dBA daily exposure with ear muffs; about 85-100 dBA with ear muffs or ear plugs); zone E below about 85 dBA for up to 8 hr.

A DANGER hazard sign shall be posted at every entrance (5.5.4.4.4.2), describing the protection required per figure 34 (5.5.4.4.4.3). Hazardous hand tools/portable equipment shall carry a hazard sign (5.5.4.4.4.4-5).

Large workspaces (no difficulty with telephone or occasional direct communication up to 4.6 m (15 ft)): 55 dBA (5.5.4.5.5). requirements.title: Vibration operational environment categories
requirements.text: Category A: strictly vibration (periodic), 0.5 to 80 Hz, X/Y/Z; criteria health, comfort, perception, performance (e.g., ground vehicles on smooth road). Category B: predominantly vibration with occasional shocks, 0.5 to 80 Hz, X/Y/Z; same criteria (off-road vehicles, severe buffeting). Category C: dominated by repeated shocks exceeding 9.81 m/s² (1 g), 0.01 to 80 Hz, vertical (Z) only; health (aircraft extreme buffeting, vessels at 20+ knots in sea state 5). Category D: low-frequency oscillatory motion at or below 0.5 Hz, 0.1 to 0.5 Hz, Z only; motion sickness (ships, undersea vehicles, spacecraft).

requirements.title: Vibration evaluation per ISO 2631-1/-5
requirements.text: Evaluation of military vehicle vibration on health, comfort, perception, performance, and motion sickness shall be in accordance with ISO 2631-1 and ISO 2631-5. Measurements (5.5.5.1.4): categories A and B triaxial at the human/source interface (seat pan for seated, floor for standing, pelvis for recumbent), 0.5 to 80 Hz, minimum 5 to 10 cycles of lowest frequency; category C Z-axis at ischial tuberosities/seat pan, 0.01 to 80 Hz; category D Z-axis 0.1 to 0.5 Hz.

requirements.text: The seat pan vector sum (vibration total value av) of the daily seated exposure within 24 hours shall not fall within the zone 'Health Risks are LIKELY' above curve A1 on figure 36. If av falls in the Caution Zone between curves A1 and A2, a warning to occupants shall be provided and attempts made to reduce exposure to below A2 (5.5.5.1.5.1.2). Allowable durations (5.5.5.1.5.1.3): t = 6/av² (curve A1) and t = 1.5/av² (curve A2). For VDV: limit 21 m/s^1.75 and action 9.1 m/s^1.75 (5.5.5.1.5.2.5).

requirements.title: Vibration performance criteria
requirements.text: Seat pan weighted triaxial RMS accelerations (any axis or vector sum) shall be limited to below curve A2 on figure 36 for the exposure duration. requirements.title: Motion sickness exposure guidance
requirements.text: Vehicles shall be designed to limit oscillatory motion in 0.1 to 0.5 Hz (5.5.5.1.9.1). Guidance: avoid exposure to problematic frequencies for longer than about 30 minutes; limit heave; avoid acceleration without an earth-fixed reference; limit MSDV to less than 30 m/s^1.5 to keep the motion sickness rate below 10 percent (Km = 1/3 for mixed un-adapted adults).

requirements.title: Vehicle seating vibration design
requirements.text: Vehicle seating systems shall minimize transmission of vibration and shock; seat resonances below 20 Hz shall be avoided (may be necessary for category C shock mitigation) (5.5.5.1.10.1); higher frequencies at seatback and headrest avoided where visual performance is critical (5.5.5.1.10.3); seats shall limit relative motion between operator and critical controls/displays (5.5.5.1.10.4, 5.5.5.3.2).

requirements.title: Vehicle seat back, buttock and leg support

requirements.title: Sustained vs transient acceleration definition
requirements.text: Sustained accelerations are events with duration of greater than or equal to 1.0 second; transient or impact accelerations are less than 1.0 second. G is the inertial resultant in multiples of g = 9.80665 m/s² (5.5.6.1). Axes (table XXIV): +Gx eyeballs-in (forward), -Gx eyeballs-out, +Gy eyeballs-left, -Gy eyeballs-right, +Gz eyeballs-down (upward accel.), -Gz eyeballs-up. Onset: gradual < 1.0 G/s, rapid 1.0 to 2.0 G/s, very high > 6.0 G/s; at +5 Gz and higher G-LOC can occur after the brain's 3 to 5 s oxygen reserve without anti-G garment and straining (5.5.6.2).

requirements.title: Physiological effects of sustained acceleration (posture/reach relevant)
requirements.text: Selected entries: +2.0 Gx tolerable at least 24 hours; +4.0 Gx tolerable up to at least 60 minutes; at +6.0 to +9.0 Gx body, legs and arms cannot be lifted at +8.0 G, head cannot be lifted at +9.0 G, precise manual control compromised. ±1.0 to 2.0 Gy: difficulty keeping head and shoulders upright without restraints, difficulty of precise manual control, head and body bracing or restraints required; ±3.0 Gy discomfort after 10 seconds, full body restraint critical. +2.0 to +2.5 Gz: difficulty using touchscreens or other precision hand/arm movements; +3.0 to +4.0 Gz: movement of extremities difficult, head movement difficult at or above +4 Gz, difficulty viewing head-down displays, grayout/tunneling; +5.0 to +6.0 Gz: blackout, G-LOC typically at +6.0 Gz or beyond, recovery up to 55 seconds; > +6.0 Gz protection needed. -1.0 Gz tolerable; -2.0 to -3.0 Gz severe facial congestion; > -3.0 Gz red-out, unconsciousness.

requirements.title: Seat head clearance to impact surface
requirements.text: A clearance measuring at least 50 mm (2 in) shall be provided between the user's head in appropriate gear and the closest potential head impact.

values.quantity: head (helmeted) to nearest hard surface clearance

requirements.site_hook: Clearance query between mannequin head (+ helmet offset) and nearest sandbox object; flag < 50 mm
requirements.percentile_rule: largest seated user in gear (sitting height P95/P97.5 M + helmet)

requirements.title: Body clearance fore-aft
requirements.text: A clearance measuring at least 50 mm (2 in) in the fore-aft direction shall be provided between any body part and any hard surface while the occupant is wearing mission clothing and equipment.
requirements.site_hook: Min distance along vehicle X between mannequin mesh (clothed) and objects; flag < 50 mm
requirements.percentile_rule: largest user in mission gear

requirements.title: Body clearance lateral
requirements.text: A clearance measuring at least 50 mm (2 in) in the horizontal direction should be provided between any body part and any hard surface with the occupant wearing mission clothing and equipment. Does not apply to occupant-to-occupant seating.
requirements.site_hook: Min lateral distance mannequin to objects; flag < 50 mm
requirements.percentile_rule: largest user in mission gear

requirements.title: Body clearance vertical
requirements.text: A clearance measuring at least 50 mm (2 in) in the vertical direction shall be provided between any body part and any hard surface with the occupant wearing mission clothing and equipment.
requirements.site_hook: Min vertical distance mannequin to objects; flag < 50 mm
requirements.percentile_rule: largest user in mission gear

requirements.title: Seat gear accommodation
requirements.text: Seats and associated clearances shall be designed to accommodate required occupant gear as specified (see 6.2).
requirements.site_hook: Gear/equipment volume add-on to mannequin (body armour, hydration pack)

requirements.title: Seat padding bottoming
requirements.text: Seat padding should be resilient enough to keep the occupant's body from contacting the seat bottom during mobility-induced loading while wearing mission clothing and equipment.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist

requirements.title: Seat back lateral support
requirements.text: The seat back should be contoured to provide lateral support to the seat occupant.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist

requirements.title: Seat drop load onto seat pan
requirements.text: Seats shall accommodate the weight of the occupant dropping from a height of 1.2 m (4 ft) onto the seat pan in any of the seat's adjustment positions while wearing mission clothing and equipment.

values.quantity: occupant drop height onto seat pan
values.condition: 4 ft; any adjustment position; occupant in mission gear

requirements.site_hook: Structural: could compute energy = mass(P99 male + gear) x g x 1.2 m for the seat object; otherwise manual
requirements.percentile_rule: heaviest occupant with gear

requirements.title: Seat drop load onto seat back
requirements.text: Seats shall accommodate the weight of the occupant dropping from a height of 1.2 m (4 ft) onto the seat back while wearing mission clothing and equipment; if the seat back folds horizontal, in any adjustment position.

values.quantity: occupant drop height onto seat back

requirements.percentile_rule: heaviest occupant with gear

requirements.title: Seats used as standing surfaces
requirements.text: Where seats can be used as standing surfaces when operating in the hatch or entryway above the seat, the seat shall accommodate the weight of the occupant wearing mission clothing and equipment in all specified vehicle mobility loading scenarios.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist; standing-on-seat posture could check head-out-of-hatch height

requirements.title: Open hatch seat emergency drop
requirements.text: All vehicles with an open-hatch or open-protected hatch seat shall provide the capability for the seat to drop immediately to allow personnel to seek protection during emergencies, including hostile fire or vehicle rollover.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist; seat travel parameter could show head below hatch rim when dropped

requirements.title: Non-skid standing surface on seat
requirements.text: If the seat surface used as the standing surface is not the seat cushion (seat back folds horizontal), the surface shall have a non-skid surface or coating.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist

requirements.title: Seats adjacent to doorways
requirements.text: Seats adjacent to doorways or entryways shall accommodate the weight of the heaviest user sliding across the seat during ingress or egress while wearing mission clothing and equipment without damage.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist
requirements.percentile_rule: heaviest user with gear

requirements.title: Seat vertical and fore/aft adjustment
requirements.text: The seat shall provide vertical (up/down) and horizontal (fore/aft) travel to accommodate the defined occupant population and allow the occupant to see, reach, and use all provided controls; see all displays; and use direct and indirect vision systems (e.g., screens, periscopes).
requirements.site_hook: Vehicle seat object with adjustment range (vertical, fore/aft); for each population case find a seat position where eye point sees displays/vision blocks and hand reach hits all controls; report required travel vs provided
requirements.percentile_rule: defined occupant population (P5F..P95M min)

requirements.title: Seat travel to open-hatch positions
requirements.text: The vertical and horizontal seat travel shall allow the occupant to reach the open-protected and open-hatch position if the vehicle is so equipped.
requirements.site_hook: Seat travel + mannequin sitting eye height: check eye/head reaches above hatch rim for smallest user at max seat height and that largest fits at lowest
requirements.percentile_rule: smallest and largest occupant

requirements.title: Seat adjustment accidental activation
requirements.text: Seat adjustment controls and mechanism shall be designed to prevent accidental activation.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist

requirements.title: Seat adjusts for egress/rescue
requirements.text: If a seat blocks an egress path or inhibits the rescue of an incapacitated seated occupant, the seat shall adjust as required in order to accommodate these scenarios.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist

requirements.title: Seat adjustment operable from in and out of seat
requirements.text: Any action required to adjust the seat to accommodate egress or rescue shall be operable by personnel who are in the seat as well as personnel who are not in the seat.
requirements.site_hook: Reach check to seat adjustment control from seated and from adjacent standing/kneeling posture

requirements.title: Single-handed seat adjustment
requirements.text: Adjustment of the seat shall not require more than a single-handed action. Two-handed action is acceptable to accommodate rescue of an incapacitated seat occupant.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist

requirements.title: Seat adjustment operable by occupant
requirements.text: The single-handed action shall be operable by the seat occupant while positioned in the seat (raising oneself to unweight the seat is permissible).
requirements.site_hook: Seated reach from mannequin to seat-adjust control location (smallest user)
requirements.percentile_rule: smallest user

requirements.title: Seat adjustment control force
requirements.text: Controls that implement the seat adjustment shall not require more than 36 newtons (8 lbs) to activate.
requirements.site_hook: Force parameter on seat adjust control; compare <= 36 N

requirements.title: Seat adjustment snag hazard
requirements.text: Controls and mechanisms that implement the seat adjustment shall not present a snag hazard during ingress or egress.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist

requirements.title: Seat adjustment control return to neutral
requirements.text: The seat adjustment control shall return to the neutral position when no force is applied to it.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist

requirements.title: Seat crush hazard
requirements.text: The seat shall not create a crush hazard between the seat and any adjacent items in the area.
requirements.site_hook: Check seat travel envelope vs adjacent objects and mannequin limbs for pinch gaps

requirements.title: Restraint latch release with gloved hand
requirements.text: The latch release mechanism for the restraint shall be able to be disengaged by the seat occupant with a single gloved hand.
requirements.site_hook: Reach check to restraint buckle location with glove; otherwise manual

requirements.title: Head restraints vs ingress/egress
requirements.text: Headrests and head restraints shall not interfere with the seat occupant's ability to ingress or egress the vehicle.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist

requirements.title: Open-hatch occupant restraint
requirements.text: An occupant in a hatch opening (standing or seated) while in a moving vehicle shall be restrained to prevent their ejection in a crash, blast, or rollover.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist

requirements.title: Bench seat spacing
requirements.text: Bench seating for embarked personnel shall provide a minimum of 550 mm (22 in), 663 mm (26.5 in) preferred, centerline-to-centerline spacing for adjacent seat positions.
requirements.site_hook: Spacing between adjacent seat objects (or seat positions on a bench); compare to clothed/equipped shoulder/elbow breadth P95M
requirements.percentile_rule: clothed & equipped bideltoid breadth, large male

requirements.title: Discrete seat spacing
requirements.text: Discrete seating for embarked personnel shall provide a minimum of 610 mm (24 in), 663 mm (26.5 in) preferred, centerline-to-centerline spacing for adjacent seat positions.
requirements.site_hook: Distance between adjacent vehicle seat object centerlines; compare
requirements.percentile_rule: clothed & equipped bideltoid breadth, large male

requirements.title: Steering wheel lateral offset from seat centerline
requirements.text: The steering mechanism (steering wheel or yoke) shall be no more than 25 mm (1 in) offset from the longitudinal centerline of the seat.

values.quantity: steering wheel offset from seat longitudinal centerline

requirements.site_hook: Lateral offset between steering wheel object centre and vehicle seat centerline; compare <= 25 mm

requirements.title: Steering force, power steering failure
requirements.text: In case of power steering failure, the operator shall not have to apply more than 220 newtons (50 lb) of force on the steering wheel in order to guide the vehicle.

values.quantity: steering wheel rim force with power steering failed

requirements.site_hook: Force parameter on steering wheel; compare <= 220 N; could compare with arm strength data for P5F

requirements.title: Brake pedal force, power brake failure
requirements.text: In case of power brake failure, the operator shall not have to apply more than 800 newtons (180 lb) of force on the brake pedal in order to stop the vehicle.

values.quantity: brake pedal force with power brake failed

requirements.site_hook: Force parameter on pedal; compare <= 800 N; leg-thrust capability depends on knee angle (seat position)

requirements.title: Pedals accept foot weight
requirements.text: Foot pedals shall accept the weight of the operator's foot without initiating control action (see 5.1.4.2.2.2 and figure 21).
requirements.site_hook: Pedal preload/resistance parameter vs foot weight (cross-ref 5.1.4.2.2.2)

requirements.title: Controls reachable while restrained
requirements.text: Controls shall be reachable while wearing safety restraints.
requirements.site_hook: Seated reach envelope with trunk restrained (shoulder fixed against seat back) to each control object; smallest user
requirements.percentile_rule: smallest user (P5F or lower), restrained

requirements.title: Weapon controls reachable while restrained
requirements.text: The placement of elevation and azimuth weapon controls shall enable the user to be restrained in his or her seat while simultaneously operating the weapons controls and interfacing with sights and other essential fire control equipment.
requirements.site_hook: Gunner posture: restrained reach to weapon controls AND eye at sight eyepiece simultaneously; all population cases
requirements.percentile_rule: full user range

requirements.title: Powered weapon controller dead spot
requirements.text: The powered weapon system controller's dead spot shall not exceed ±2 degrees in each direction from the center position.
requirements.site_hook: Controller parameter; compare

requirements.title: Trigger guard
requirements.text: A trigger guard(s) shall be provided to prevent inadvertent operation of the trigger(s).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist

requirements.title: Dead man switch
requirements.text: A dead man-type safety switch shall be provided that requires the weapon station operator's continued activation while providing weapon station movement and firing input; release shall cease movement and firing (5.6.3.2.7).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist

requirements.title: Powered weapon controls either hand
requirements.text: For the crewmember with primary responsibility for weapon system operation, powered weapon system controls should be operable with either hand.
requirements.site_hook: Reach with left and right hand to controller

requirements.title: Indirect-vision driver display distance
requirements.text: The driver's display used for driving via indirect vision should be located not less than 38 mm (15 in) from the driver' eye point and within reach of the driver. [As printed: 38 mm vs 15 in are inconsistent; 15 in = 381 mm.]

values.quantity: display distance from driver eye point
values.condition: as printed; customary value 15 in (=381 mm) suggests a typo

values.quantity: display distance from driver eye point

requirements.site_hook: Eye-to-display viewing distance tool: compare >= 15 in (381 mm) and hand reach to display; flag the typo
requirements.percentile_rule: driver population range

requirements.title: Indirect-vision driver display lateral position
requirements.text: The driver's primary display used for driving via indirect vision should be centered on the longitudinal centerline of the seat.

values.quantity: display centre lateral offset from seat centerline

requirements.site_hook: Lateral offset display centre vs seat centerline

requirements.title: Indirect-vision driver display vertical angle
requirements.text: The driver's display used for driving via indirect vision should be located between 0 and 15 degrees below the horizontal line of sight.

values.quantity: display angle below horizontal line of sight

requirements.site_hook: Viewing angle below horizontal tool from mannequin eye to display centre; compare 0-15 deg for P5F and P95M seat positions
requirements.percentile_rule: small and large driver

requirements.title: Rollover indicator visible
requirements.text: A rollover indicator, if provided, shall be visible to the driver.
requirements.site_hook: Line-of-sight check from driver eye to indicator object

requirements.title: Field of regard criteria are minimums
requirements.text: Horizontal and vertical fields of regard in 5.6.5.2-5.6.5.7 are minimums (wider preferred); ground intercept values are maximums (closer preferred). Figures 41-46 depict the criteria (range ring interval = 2 m).
requirements.site_hook: Vision analysis module: from mannequin eye point(s) compute horizontal FOR (azimuth unobstructed) and ground intercept distance against vehicle body/window geometry

requirements.title: Windshield station driver horizontal FOR
requirements.text: The horizontal field of regard from the driver's station shall be at least 180 degrees, 220 degrees preferred, with at least 90 degrees to either side of the driver's seat longitudinal centerline (see figure 41; figure shows driver preferred sector 250 deg to 110 deg).

values.quantity: FOR each side of seat centerline

requirements.site_hook: Compute unobstructed azimuth sweep from mannequin eye point through vehicle window/vision device geometry; compare
requirements.percentile_rule: driver/commander eye point for small and large users

requirements.title: Windshield station field restriction
requirements.text: Within the horizontal field of regard, not more than 15 degrees of non-contiguous field of regard shall be blocked due to cab structure or headlights, mirrors, or other externally mounted components.
requirements.site_hook: Sum angular width of obstructions (pillars, mirrors) seen from eye point within FOR; compare <= 15 deg
requirements.percentile_rule: driver/commander eye point for small and large users

requirements.title: Windshield station combined FOR
requirements.text: The combined horizontal field of regard from the driver's and a second crewmember's stations shall be at least 220 degrees (see figure 41).
requirements.site_hook: Union of azimuth sectors from two mannequin eye points; compare
requirements.percentile_rule: driver/commander eye point for small and large users

requirements.title: Windshield station vertical FOR
requirements.text: The vertical field of regard shall be at least 15 degrees above the horizontal plane associated with the driver's eye point.

values.quantity: vertical FOR above horizontal at eye point

requirements.site_hook: Angle from eye point to top windshield edge/roof line; compare >= 15 deg
requirements.percentile_rule: tall driver (P95M+ sitting eye height) is the limiting case

requirements.title: Windshield station ground intercept
requirements.text: The vertical field of regard shall enable the driver to view the ground 3 m (10 ft) in front of the front surface of the vehicle in line with the driver's seat longitudinal centerline. Mirrors or vision enhancers may be used if tactical requirements permit.

values.quantity: ground intercept ahead of vehicle front surface

requirements.site_hook: Ray from eye point over hood/lower window edge to ground plane; intercept distance ahead of vehicle front surface on station centerline; compare <= value
requirements.percentile_rule: short driver (P5F sitting eye height) is the limiting case

requirements.title: Vehicles with trailers
requirements.text: For vehicles with trailers, the driver shall be able to observe at least portions of the trailer and the load.
requirements.site_hook: Line of sight from eye point (via mirror) to trailer object
requirements.percentile_rule: driver/commander eye point for small and large users

requirements.title: Windshield obstructions without moving
requirements.text: Door posts, windshield wiper motors, and other devices shall not require the driver to move from his or her normal restrained seated position to view around an obstruction. A narrow corner post is preferable to a wraparound windshield.
requirements.site_hook: Visibility analysis from fixed restrained eye point (no head translation)
requirements.percentile_rule: driver/commander eye point for small and large users

requirements.title: Visors against glare
requirements.text: Visors or other means shall be used to preclude performance degradation due to glare from external sources such as sunlight or headlights.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist

requirements.title: Interior surfaces/displays reflected glare
requirements.text: Interior surfaces (5.6.5.2.12) and interior displays (5.6.5.2.13) shall be designed/located to reduce reflected glare into the driver's eyes or onto the windshield.
requirements.site_hook: Specular reflection ray check display -> windshield -> eye point

requirements.title: Open hatch driver horizontal FOR
requirements.text: From the open-hatch position, the horizontal field of regard from the driver's station shall be at least 180 degrees, with at least 90 degrees to either side of the longitudinal centerline through the driver's station (see figure 42).

values.quantity: FOR each side of station centerline

requirements.site_hook: Compute unobstructed azimuth sweep from mannequin eye point through vehicle window/vision device geometry; compare

requirements.text: If an occupant can easily place feet on a non-protected area while sitting, it shall be labeled with a NO FEET warning.
requirements.site_hook: Foot reach zone from seat vs floor areas

requirements.title: Equipment storage / tie-downs
requirements.text: Vehicles shall provide storage, weapon mounts, and tie-downs to prevent loose gear from becoming projectiles in a blast or collision.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist

requirements.title: Power door crush sensor response
requirements.text: Crush sensors shall cause the power-operated door to stop closing within 1 second and automatically reverse to open the door by 5 to 10 degrees angularly or 150 mm (6 in) linearly; trigger after 1 kg (2.2 lb) of pressure (5.6.9.11.4).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist / spec entry

requirements.title: Stowed gear vs clearances and egress
requirements.text: Stowed gear and equipment shall not prevent meeting the vehicle's operational clearances or the ingress and egress requirements of 5.6.8; stowage provisions likewise (5.6.10.2).
requirements.site_hook: Stowage box objects included in clearance/egress path checks

requirements.title: Drains reachable without removing components
requirements.text: Drains shall be located where crewmembers can clear and check them without removing components (opening an access panel is not removing a component).
requirements.site_hook: Maintainer reach to drain locations

requirements.title: Dipstick location
requirements.text: Dipsticks shall be located where crewmembers can check and top off fluid levels without powering up the vehicle and without removing components.
requirements.site_hook: Standing/kneeling reach to dipstick location

requirements.title: Power receptacle accessible from ground
requirements.text: Subordinate power receptacles shall be accessible to all personnel from ground level; otherwise footholds and handholds per 5.6.8.6 (5.6.11.4.5).
requirements.site_hook: Standing reach of smallest user from ground to receptacle object
requirements.percentile_rule: smallest user

requirements.title: Battery servicing by one person
requirements.text: Batteries shall be capable of servicing, installation, and removal by one person without removing other items or special tools.
requirements.site_hook: Battery mass and lift geometry vs one-person lift limits (5.20)

requirements.title: Fuel fill port reachable from ground
requirements.text: Fuel fill ports should be accessible by the user while standing on the ground; otherwise footholds/handholds per 5.6.8.6 shall be provided (5.6.11.5.3).
requirements.site_hook: Standing reach of smallest user to fill port object
requirements.percentile_rule: smallest user

requirements.title: Fuel drains accessible
requirements.text: Fuel system drains shall be accessible by the user population in appropriate clothing and gear without powering up or removing components.
requirements.site_hook: Maintainer reach

requirements.title: Belt adjustment in arctic mittens
requirements.text: Fan belts and other drives requiring adjustment should be designed to be handled while wearing arctic mittens and located/protected from burn hazards.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist

requirements.title: Daily-check access panels single operator
requirements.text: Hoods and access panels opened for daily checks should be accessible and operable by a single operator.
requirements.site_hook: Reach to hood latch / lift force

requirements.title: Tarpaulin removal time
requirements.text: Tarpaulins, camouflage systems, end curtains, and bows should be removable/installable by two crewmembers in 10 minutes or less (not arctic enclosures).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist

requirements.title: Hydraulic line marking interval
requirements.text: Inlets, outlets, and connecting lines in hydraulic systems shall be identified at least every 450 mm (18 in) and at both ends.
requirements.site_hook: Not body-related

requirements.title: Transportable enclosure ceiling height
requirements.text: For transportable enclosures occupied > 1 hour, the ceiling height (floor to bottom of any light, cable run, or protuberance over the aisle or standing workspace) shall be not less than 198 cm (78 in).
requirements.site_hook: Ceiling/overhead object height; compare; also stature P99M + helmet/shoes
requirements.percentile_rule: tall male

requirements.title: Reduced enclosure ceiling height
requirements.text: Unless otherwise specified, when occupants seldom stand to perform normal operations, the ceiling height can be reduced to 189 cm (74.5 in).
requirements.site_hook: Ceiling height alternative threshold

requirements.title: Enclosure personnel access opening
requirements.text: Personnel access openings should be not less than 173 cm (69 in) high and 75 cm (30 in) wide.
requirements.site_hook: Door object height/width; compare

requirements.title: Equipment access openings
requirements.text: Equipment access openings shall accommodate the specific equipment to be transported, including clearances for handling.
requirements.site_hook: Box object dims + hand clearance vs opening

requirements.title: Enclosure steps when floor > 46 cm
requirements.text: Steps, stairs, or ladders shall be provided when transportable enclosure floors are more than 46 cm (18 in) above ground level (see 5.11.8).

values.quantity: enclosure floor height above ground triggering steps

requirements.site_hook: Floor height; flag if > 46 cm without stair/ladder object

requirements.title: Enclosure inclinometers
requirements.text: Inclinometers shall permit readout of front-rear and side-side tilt within ±2 degrees, visible and readable from the ground (5.6.11.13.7.2).
requirements.site_hook: Line of sight from standing ground eye height to inclinometer

requirements.title: Crane/handling operator load visibility
requirements.text: The workstation shall be designed to ensure that the operator has visibility of the load at all times; controls within reach and affording visibility of the load (5.6.11.14.3).
requirements.site_hook: Line-of-sight from operator eye point to load/hook object + reach to controls

requirements.title: Construction machinery access dimensions
requirements.text: Unless otherwise specified, access dimensions for construction machinery shall be in accordance with SAE J925, as applicable; handholds and footholds per 5.6.8.6 (5.6.11.14.9).
requirements.site_hook: External standard (SAE J925)

requirements.title: Forklift fork tip visibility
requirements.text: Forklift configuration shall permit the operator direct view of the tips of the forks in all typical loading modes and operator positions.
requirements.site_hook: Line-of-sight from seated operator eye (P5F & P95M) to fork tip objects past mast
requirements.percentile_rule: full operator range

requirements.title: Small jacks one-person carry
requirements.text: Small jacks shall be designed to be lifted and carried by one person (see 5.20.3).
requirements.site_hook: Mass vs one-person lift limit

requirements.title: Winch controls with arctic mittens
requirements.text: Winch controls at the winch shall be capable of being operated by personnel wearing arctic mittens.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist

requirements.title: Hoist control box handheld
requirements.text: The hoist control box shall be lightweight and handheld so the operator may reach the up and down control while holding the box securely and comfortably.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist

requirements.title: Hazard-alerting device
requirements.text: An auditory and visual hazard-alerting device shall be provided to warn personnel of impending danger or existing hazards (e.g., fire, combustible or asphyxiating gas, smoke, radiation); it shall be perceptible in all expected ambient noise/ear covering (5.7.5.1.1) and lighting (5.7.5.1.2) conditions and not be confused with other alarms (5.7.5.1.3).
requirements.site_hook: Not geometric; out of scope for the site except as a facility checklist item.

requirements.title: Emergency egress routes accommodate population
requirements.text: Design of emergency egress routes, markings, and related hardware (doors and openings) shall conform to life safety codes and accommodate the intended population and number of occupants, including mobility hampered personnel, if appropriate (guidance NFPA 101; see 5.11.7.4).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist; door/opening widths can be checked against 5.11.7.4 and 5.11.3.2 items.

requirements.title: Maintenance workspace free of obstructions
requirements.text: The workspace around areas where maintenance is performed shall be free of obstructions that could cause injury, through accidental contact or because the obstruction requires an awkward or dangerous body position.
requirements.site_hook: Place mannequin in maintenance posture near equipment; flag mannequin-object collisions and high RULA/REBA scores caused by obstructions.

requirements.title: Overhead mounted items minimum height
requirements.text: Pipe hangers or any other item mounted in the overhead of passageways, walkways, or other dedicated walking areas shall not protrude below 203 cm (80 in) (213 cm [84 in] preferred) above the walking surface.

values.quantity: height of lowest point of overhead-mounted item above walking surface

requirements.title: Bulkhead mounting zones for pipe hangers/wireways
requirements.text: Items (e.g., pipe hangers) mounted to bulkheads to support pipe or wireways shall be placed only in the areas shown on figure 47 (5.7.5.5.2): from 965 mm (38 in) to 1346 mm (53 in), or at 1956 mm (77 in) and above. Dimensions measured from the walking surface.

requirements.title: Storage racks not impede traffic
requirements.text: Storage racks located in passageways and secured to bulkheads (gas bottles, casualty cables, firefighting equipment, etc.) shall not impede traffic flow.

requirements.title: Storage racks no protruding studs or sharp corners
requirements.text: Storage racks located in passageways and secured to bulkheads shall not have securing studs or other sharp objects (e.g., corners) protruding into the passageway.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist.

requirements.title: Cabinet door swing not interfering with passage
requirements.text: Hinges for doors on lockers, electrical cabinets, storage bins, equipment lockers, or other spaces shall be located so that a partially- or fully-opened door will not interfere with personnel or equipment flow or cause injury to personnel moving past. Accordion, rolling (garage door type), or other non-protruding doors may be considered.
requirements.site_hook: Door object swing arc vs passageway clear width; would need a cabinet-door swing path in the sandbox.

requirements.title: Illumination of all areas, stairways and hazardous areas
requirements.text: Illumination shall be provided in all areas, including storage areas (5.7.5.8.1). Warning placards, stairways, and all hazardous areas shall be illuminated in accordance with 5.5.3 (5.7.5.8.2).
requirements.site_hook: User enters illuminance level for stair/hazard areas; compare with 5.5.3 tables.

requirements.title: Surface temperature exposure limits (guarding)
requirements.text: Equipment that exposes personnel to surface temperatures greater than those in table XXVII or less than 0 °C (32 °F) in normal operation shall be guarded. Table XXVII: momentary contact - metal 60 °C (140 °F), glass 68 °C (154 °F), plastic or wood 85 °C (185 °F); prolonged contact or handling - metal 49 °C (120 °F), glass 59 °C (138 °F), plastic or wood 69 °C (156 °F). Climate-induced surface temperatures are exempt.

requirements.title: Low heat conductivity of touched surfaces

requirements.title: Hot metal surfaces 49 °C precautions
requirements.text: If personnel can touch metal surfaces that may get as hot as 49 °C (120 °F), special precautions shall be incorporated, such as shielding, insulating, PPE (gloves), relocating components, or adding warning decals, signs, or labels. Figure 48 shows burn criteria for human skin.

requirements.title: Burn criteria for human skin
requirements.text: Graph of skin temperature (40-70 °C) vs exposure duration (0.1 s to about 7 h, log scale) showing pain threshold line, 1st degree burn curve and 2nd degree burn curve (irreversible tissue damage above). requirements.title: Safety barriers
requirements.text: Safety barriers shall be used to protect a person from contacting a hazard (e.g., rotating machinery, electrical contact, hot pipe) as shown on figure 49.

requirements.title: Safety barrier height / distance table
requirements.text: Figure 49 table gives the horizontal distance 'A' (mm) from the danger point required for a barrier with edge height 'B' (2,400 (94.7 in) to 1,000 (39.5 in) mm) and danger point height from floor 'C' (2,400 (94.7 in) to 200 (7.9 in) mm). There should be no interpolation of the values. Examples: C = 1,500 mm, A = 700 mm -> B should be 1,800 mm; B = 1,300 mm, C = 2,300 mm -> A = 600 mm; B = 1,700 mm, A = 550 mm -> danger point should not be between 1,200 and 2,200 mm. Cells printed '--' carry no distance (B=2,400 column is '--' for all C; the lower-left cells where C is well below B are '--'). Inch equivalents printed in the table are kept in the source; e.g. 100 (3.9), 250 (9.9), 350 (13.8), 400 (15.8), 500 (19.7), 600 (23.7), 700 (27.6), 800 (31.6), 900 (35.5), 1,000 (39.5), 1,100 (43.4), 1,200 (47.4), 1,300 (51.3), 1,400 (55.3), 300 (11.8), 200 (7.9).
