requirements.percentile_rule: based on male data

requirements.title: Whole body access - side access openings
requirements.text: Side access: light clothing A 660 mm (26 in), B 760 mm (30 in); bulky clothing A 740 mm (29 in), B 860 mm (34 in). A is opening height, B is opening width (as drawn). Dimensions are based on male data.
requirements.site_hook: Sandbox access opening (vertical wall) height/width vs table; kneeling/crawling mannequin pass-through.
requirements.percentile_rule: based on male data

requirements.title: Glass doors patterned
requirements.text: Where floor-to-ceiling doors or windows are used, the glass area shall be patterned or labeled so users do not mistake it for an unobstructed passageway.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist.

requirements.title: Emergency exit space for occupants with equipment
requirements.text: Emergency exits shall allow enough space for rapid exit of all occupants, including any who carry essential equipment or wear bulky clothing, without injury or equipment damage (29 CFR 1910.36, 1910.37, NFPA).
requirements.site_hook: Exit opening vs clothed P99 mannequin + carried box.

requirements.title: Emergency exit design criteria (qualitative)
requirements.text: Emergency doors and exits shall be simple to operate, readily accessible, clearly designated, unobstructed, simple to locate and operate in the dark, and not in themselves constitute a safety hazard.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist.

requirements.title: Emergency exit opening time
requirements.text: Emergency doors and exits shall be capable of being opened in 3 seconds or less (item f).
requirements.site_hook: User-entered test time.

requirements.title: Emergency exit operating force
requirements.text: Emergency doors and exits shall require from 44 to 133 newtons (10 to 30 pounds-force) of operating force to open (item g).
requirements.site_hook: User-entered force on door object; compare with strength data.

requirements.title: Emergency exit egress time per person
requirements.text: Emergency doors and exits shall permit exit by one person in 5 seconds or less (item h).

values.quantity: time for one person to exit

requirements.site_hook: User-entered test time.

requirements.title: Ceiling height along means of exit
requirements.text: Ceiling areas along a means of exit (including exterior escape paths) shall be at least 2.29 m (7.5 ft) above the floor.

values.quantity: ceiling height along means of exit

requirements.site_hook: Ceiling/overhead object height; compare with P99 stature.

requirements.title: Protrusion height along means of exit
requirements.text: Protrusions along a means of exit shall be not lower than 2.04 m (6.7 ft) above the floor.

values.quantity: lowest protrusion height along means of exit

requirements.site_hook: Bottom height of overhead objects over exit route vs floor.

requirements.title: Unobstructed way-of-exit width
requirements.text: A designated means of emergency exit shall have a minimum of 460 mm (18 in) of unobstructed way-of-exit travel from any point in a structure to an exterior safe public way.
requirements.site_hook: Minimum clear width along an exit route between objects.

requirements.title: Hatches flush and single-motion
requirements.text: Where structure permits, hatches shall be flush with floor or wall surfaces; hatches shall open with a single motion of the hand or foot (5.11.7.5.2).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist.

requirements.title: Hatch handle operating force
requirements.text: When a handle is used, the hatch operating force shall not exceed 90 newtons (20 pounds-force).
requirements.site_hook: User-entered force on hatch object; compare with P5 strength.

requirements.title: Overhead hatch operating force
requirements.text: Overhead hatches shall require an operating force of less than 220 newtons (50 pounds-force) for opening and closing.
requirements.site_hook: User-entered force.

requirements.title: Hatch/passage clearance dimensions (central 98 %)
requirements.text: Clearance dimensions for hatch and passage sizes shall be based on the multivariate central 98 percent of the male and of the female target user population, using applicable dimensions, and shall accommodate suitably clothed and equipped personnel with any carried equipment (size for the largest people).
requirements.site_hook: Access-opening/hatch object vs clothed P99 mannequin passing through (shoulder breadth, chest depth, hip breadth, plus clothing/equipment allowance).
requirements.percentile_rule: multivariate central 98 % of male and of female populations (largest users drive clearance)

requirements.title: Hatch location/operability limiting dimensions (central 98 %)
requirements.text: Limiting dimensions for hatch location and operability shall be based on the multivariate central 98 percent of the male and of the female target user population, so smaller people can manipulate latches, handles, or accesses.
requirements.site_hook: Hatch latch/handle position vs P1/P5 female reach envelope (overhead and forward reach).
requirements.percentile_rule: multivariate central 98 % of male and of female populations (smallest users drive reach)

requirements.title: Emergency escape hatch accommodation and placement
requirements.text: Emergency escape hatches shall accommodate the equipment and clothing escaping personnel will carry and wear, be clear of all external obstructions, and be located to avoid external hazards.
requirements.site_hook: Hatch object vs clothed mannequin + equipment.

requirements.title: Emergency escape hatch dimensions - rectangular
requirements.text: Rectangular emergency escape hatches: minimum 405 by 610 mm (16 by 24 in), preferred 510 by 710 mm (20 by 30 in).
requirements.site_hook: Sandbox access opening/hatch width and height.

requirements.title: Emergency escape hatch dimensions - square
requirements.text: Square emergency escape hatches: minimum 460 mm (18 in), preferred 560 mm (22 in).
requirements.site_hook: Sandbox access opening/hatch width and height.

requirements.title: Overhead emergency hatch force
requirements.text: If emergency hatches must be placed overhead, they shall require no more than 220 newtons (50 pounds-force) of force to operate.
requirements.site_hook: User-entered force.

requirements.title: Emergency hatch operable by 5th percentile strength
requirements.text: Emergency escape hatches shall be operable by a suitably equipped and clothed user with fifth percentile arm and hand strength of the expected user population.

requirements.percentile_rule: fifth percentile arm and hand strength of expected user population

requirements.title: Hatch large enough for two rescuers
requirements.text: Where rescue of personnel may be required, hatch openings shall be large enough to accommodate two suitably clothed rescuers.
requirements.site_hook: Two clothed P99 mannequins fit test through opening.

requirements.title: Step-down through access opening
requirements.text: Where there is a need to step down through an access and the step distance exceeds 690 mm (27 in), footrests or steps shall be provided.

values.quantity: step-down distance through access without footrest/step

requirements.site_hook: Height from opening sill to floor below; flag > 690 mm without step object.

requirements.title: Select safest passage structure
requirements.text: The structure that gives the safest and most efficient passage shall be selected; selection of ramps, stairs, stair-ladders, or fixed ladders shall be based on the angle of ascent and table XXXIV (5.11.8.1.2).
requirements.site_hook: Compute angle of ascent from stair/ladder geometry and classify with Table XXXIV.

requirements.title: Angle of ascent - Vertical ladders
requirements.text: Vertical ladders: angle of ascent 75 to 90 degrees; preferred angle of ascent 90 (degrees).
requirements.site_hook: Ladder object inclination angle.

requirements.title: Angle of ascent - Inclined stairs
requirements.text: Inclined stairs: angle of ascent 50 to 75 degrees; preferred angle of ascent Not recommended (degrees).
requirements.site_hook: Stair object angle = atan(rise/tread); 50-75 deg classed as inclined stair (stair ladder); preferred 'Not recommended'.

requirements.title: Angle of ascent - Stairs
requirements.text: Stairs: angle of ascent 30 to 50 degrees; preferred angle of ascent 38 (degrees).
requirements.site_hook: Stair object angle = atan(riser/tread).

requirements.title: Angle of ascent - Ramps for personnel
requirements.text: Ramps for personnel: angle of ascent 7 to 15 degrees; preferred angle of ascent 7 to 8 (degrees).

requirements.site_hook: Ramp angle (needs ramp object; preferred 7 to 8 deg).

requirements.title: Angle of ascent - Ramps for material handling
requirements.text: Ramps for material handling: angle of ascent 4 to 7 degrees; preferred angle of ascent 4 (degrees).

values.quantity: angle of ascent, ramps for material handling

requirements.site_hook: Ramp angle (needs ramp object).

requirements.title: No stairs for heavy/bulky hand-carried loads
requirements.text: Stairs and steps should not be used where personnel must carry bulky loads or loads in excess of 13 kg (29 lbs); ramps, elevators, or equivalent should be provided.
requirements.site_hook: Box object mass carried by mannequin in stair-climbing posture; flag > 13 kg or bulky.

requirements.title: No ladders when carrying equipment
requirements.text: Ladders shall not be used when personnel must carry equipment because both hands should be free to grasp and climb ladders.
requirements.site_hook: Flag ladder-climbing posture combined with any carried object.

requirements.title: Materials of ramps, stairs, ladders
requirements.text: Ramps, stairs, and ladders shall be lightweight, nonconductive, splinter-proof, waterproof, weatherproof, humidity- and chemical-resistant; environmental conditions considered; tolerant of hot-water/steam de-icing if applicable.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist.

requirements.title: Load capacity of ramps, stairs, ladders
requirements.text: Ramps, stairs, and ladders shall withstand the total weight of the largest combination of personnel and carried equipment likely at one time, times a safety factor; use 113.4 kg (250 lb) per person.
requirements.site_hook: User-entered rating vs occupants x 113.4 kg + loads.

requirements.title: Non-skid surfaces on ramps, stairs, ladders
requirements.text: Ramps, stairs, and ladders shall be provided with non-skid surfaces on all areas where personnel walk or stand to work.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist.

requirements.title: Warning labels on ramps, stairs, ladders
requirements.text: Ramps, stairs, and ladders shall have labels or symbols warning of hazards (low overhead obstructions, possible shock, load limits); ladder labels per ANSI/ASC A14 (5.11.8.1.7.1); ramp and stair labels per ANSI Z535.2 (5.11.8.1.7.2).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist.

requirements.title: Handrail on each side
requirements.text: Ramps, stairs, and ladders shall be equipped with a handrail on each side.
requirements.site_hook: Stair/ladder object handrail flags (left/right).

requirements.title: Intermediate guardrail where fall into open area
requirements.text: Where personnel could fall into an open area under a catwalk, balcony, parapet, ramp, stair, or ladder handrail, an intermediate level guardrail shall be provided.
requirements.site_hook: Stair/platform object mid-rail flag.

requirements.title: Illumination of ramps, stairs, ladders
requirements.text: Ramps, stairs, and ladders shall be provided with appropriate illumination (see 5.5.3).
requirements.site_hook: User-entered illuminance.

requirements.title: Stairs alongside shared vehicle ramps over 7 degrees
requirements.text: Stairs should be provided for personnel when vehicles and pedestrians share a ramp and the ramp inclination exceeds 7 degrees (figure 84 shows ramp-and-stairs combination with pedestrian area on the right side). Personnel areas should be to one side or both sides of the vehicle area (5.11.8.1.12) and clearly separated by markings and handrails (5.11.8.1.13).

requirements.title: Ramp landings at top and bottom

requirements.site_hook: Checklist.

requirements.text: Fixed ladder dimensions shall be per figure 88 (5.11.8.5.1.1). A: rung thickness - wood minimum 32 mm (1.1 in), maximum 38 mm (1.5 in), preferred 35 mm (1.4 in); protected metal minimum 19 mm (0.8 in), maximum 38 mm (1.5 in), preferred 35 mm (1.4 in); corrosive metal minimum 25 mm (1 in), maximum 38 mm (1.5 in), preferred 35 mm (1.4 in).
requirements.site_hook: Sandbox ladder rung diameter + material selection.

requirements.title: Fixed ladder rung spacing
requirements.text: B: rung spacing minimum 230 mm (9 in), maximum 300 mm (12 in), preferred 300 mm (12 in).

requirements.text: C: height, rung to landing minimum 150 mm (6 in), maximum 380 mm (15 in), preferred 380 mm (15 in).

requirements.title: Fixed ladder width between stringers
requirements.text: D: width between stringers minimum 400 mm (16 in), maximum 400 mm (16 in), preferred 400 mm (16 in).

requirements.text: E: climbing clearance width minimum 610 mm (24 in), preferred 760 mm (30 in).

requirements.title: Fixed ladder clearance in back of ladder
requirements.text: F: clearance depth in back of ladder minimum 200 mm (8 in), preferred 200 mm (8 in).
requirements.site_hook: Distance from rung to wall behind ladder; compare with foot length for toe clearance.

requirements.title: Fixed ladder clearance on climbing side
requirements.text: G: clearance depth on climbing side (range) minimum of 910 mm (36 in) for 75°, to 760 mm (30 in) for 90°.

requirements.title: Fixed ladder stringer height above landing
requirements.text: H: height of stringer above landing minimum 1,067 mm (42 in), preferred 1,067 mm (42 in).

requirements.title: Landing platform when step-off distance large
requirements.text: Landing platforms shall be provided when the stepping distance from the centerline of a ladder rung to the nearest edge of a structure or equipment is greater than 300 mm (12 in).

requirements.title: Guardrails at multi-floor ladder landings
requirements.text: When fixed ladders are used between several floors, landings and entrances should have guardrails, especially if the ladder well is open.

requirements.title: Cages or fall-arrest for ladders over 6.1 m
requirements.text: OSHA-compliant hands-free ladder safety devices or cages complying with figure 89 shall be provided for fixed ladders over 6.1 m (20 ft) long; cage inside free of obstructions (5.11.8.5.1.8).

values.quantity: fixed ladder length above which cage/safety device required

requirements.title: Rung ladders for occasional traffic only
requirements.text: Rung ladders are acceptable for occasional traffic but shall not be used for frequent passage (dimensions in figure 89).

requirements.title: Ladder cage dimensions
requirements.text: Figure 89 (preferred values): A height of cage from base of ladder 2.1 m (6.8 ft); B flare at bottom of cage 800 mm (32 in); C depth of cage from center of ladder 710 mm (28 in); D maximum distance between cage ribs 460 mm (18 in); E width of cage 680 mm (27 in).

requirements.title: Rung ladder maximum length
requirements.text: H maximum ladder length: single ladders 9.1 m (30 ft); two-section metal ladders 14.6 m (48 ft); two-section wood ladders 18.3 m (60 ft).

requirements.title: Level steps on ladders with handrails
requirements.text: Rungs provide better hand holds than steps, but when handrails are provided on both sides, level steps 75 to 100 mm (3 to 4 in) wide should be used; rungs should have non-skid surfaces (5.11.8.5.1.10); tread rise should be open in the rear (5.11.8.5.1.11).

requirements.title: Portable ladder use restricted
requirements.text: Portable ladders should be restricted to emergency functions, infrequent maintenance, or where fixed ladders are impractical; 29 CFR 1910.25-1910.29 provide guidance (5.11.8.5.2.2).

requirements.title: Portable stepladder side-rail spread
requirements.text: Portable stepladder dimensions shall be within figure 90 (5.11.8.5.2.3). A: spread between side rails - from top to bottom, increase a minimum of 30 mm (1.25 in) per 300 mm (12 in) of side rail length.

requirements.text: D: width between side rails at top step minimum 300 mm (12 in).

requirements.text: E: width at bottom - add 30 mm (1.25 in) per foot of length (minimum).

requirements.title: Ladder weight for one-person lift and store
requirements.text: Where one person is to lift ladders and store them by hand, ladder weights shall not exceed 9 kg (20 lb) for a lift distance of 1.8 m (6 ft) or 11.3 kg (25 lb) for a lift distance of 1.5 m (5 ft).
requirements.site_hook: Ladder object mass (user entry) + lift height to storage.

requirements.title: Portable ladder feet
requirements.text: Ladders should be provided with rubber-cleated pivoted feet for nonfreezing weather and steel cleats for ice and snow.

requirements.title: Surface colors - Army and Navy
requirements.text: Army: unless otherwise specified, surface colors should use the guidance of MIL-HDBK-1473. Navy: surface colors shall be as specified (5.11.9.2).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist.

requirements.title: Surface colors - Air Force (SAE AMS-STD-595)
requirements.text: Air Force surface colors shall be selected from SAE AMS-STD-595: console, rack, cabinet exteriors 24300 Green; panels 26492 Gray; non-critical functional grouping pads 26622 Gray; emergency or critical grouping pads 21136 Red; interior walls and ceilings 27875 White; interiors of uninhabited compartments where maintenance is performed 26622 Gray; standard commercial equipment existing color (identical/compatible if integral to an assembly); anodized or conductive surface not painted. Lettering (background/lettering): 24300 Green/17875 White; 26492 Gray/17038 Black; 27875 White/17038 Black; 26231 Gray/17875 White; 21136 Red/17875 White; anodized or non-painted 17038 Black or 17875 White whichever gives better contrast; commercial equipment contrasting color.
requirements.site_hook: Object colour attribute vs allowed FED-STD-595 code list (Air Force mode).

requirements.section_title: Virtual environments, remote, automated and unmanned systems
requirements.title: VE physical barriers
requirements.text: VE workstations shall have physical barriers preventing persons in a VE from wandering into hazards or becoming entangled in or constrained by cabling.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist

requirements.section_title: Virtual environments, remote, automated and unmanned systems
requirements.title: VE exclusion zone
requirements.text: An equipment-, personnel-, and obstruction-free exclusion zone not less than 1 m (39 in) beyond each edge of the interactive area shall be provided for all immersive VE applications when the operator is not seated or constrained.

values.quantity: exclusion zone beyond interactive area edge

requirements.site_hook: Floor area object for VE play space; check no sandbox objects within 1 m of its edges; could also compare arm-span reach envelope

requirements.section_title: Virtual environments, remote, automated and unmanned systems
requirements.title: VE floors flat and level
requirements.text: Floors and walkways shall be flat and level; ramps, steps and grade changes should be minimized (5.12.1.3.2.2).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist

requirements.section_title: Virtual environments, remote, automated and unmanned systems
requirements.title: VE system transport delay
requirements.text: System transport delays between user input and system output should not exceed 100 milliseconds (preferred range: 20 to 50 milliseconds) roundtrip.
requirements.site_hook: Not geometric; spec entry

requirements.section_title: Virtual environments, remote, automated and unmanned systems
requirements.title: HMD latency
requirements.text: HMD latencies shall be not longer than 150 milliseconds (50 milliseconds preferred) without an evaluation in a representative environment; for large-FOV HMDs in precision applications latency shall be not longer than 20 milliseconds.
requirements.site_hook: Spec entry

requirements.section_title: Virtual environments, remote, automated and unmanned systems
requirements.title: HMD update rate
requirements.text: For head-mounted displays, the scene update rate shall be at least 60 hertz; for critical fast-motion applications total latency not greater than 20 milliseconds and update rates should be at least 100 hertz (5.12.1.4.4); avoid flicker 1 to 30 hertz (5.12.1.4.2).
requirements.site_hook: Spec entry

requirements.section_title: Virtual environments, remote, automated and unmanned systems
requirements.title: Body-referenced interface latency
requirements.text: Human interfaces to robotic systems employing body-referenced interfaces shall have latencies below 50 milliseconds.
requirements.site_hook: Spec entry

requirements.section_title: Virtual environments, remote, automated and unmanned systems
requirements.title: Remote surveillance display update
requirements.text: For remote surveillance systems, the display shall update no later than 200 milliseconds from user command.
requirements.site_hook: Spec entry

requirements.section_title: Virtual environments, remote, automated and unmanned systems
requirements.title: Manipulator type by load (< 10 kg)
requirements.text: For tasks requiring manipulative dexterity and load capacities of less than 10 kg (22 lb), manipulators shall provide position control, mutual force reflection, and appropriate DOF; for gross positioning of loads equal to or heavier than 10 kg (22 lb), powered manipulators with rate control shall be provided (5.12.2.4.3).

values.quantity: load threshold position vs rate control

requirements.site_hook: Spec entry

requirements.section_title: Virtual environments, remote, automated and unmanned systems
requirements.title: Remote display lettering size
requirements.text: Letters and numbers on an electronic display shall be a minimum 12-point sans-serif font at highest practical contrast, assuming a viewing distance of approximately 70 cm (28 in); scale for greater distance to maintain visual angle.

values.condition: at ~70 cm viewing distance; scale proportionally

requirements.site_hook: Eye-to-display distance tool: required font pt = 12 x (distance / 70 cm); compare with display text size parameter

requirements.section_title: Virtual environments, remote, automated and unmanned systems
requirements.title: Stereo display depth limit
requirements.text: The amount of depth in front of and behind the stereoscopic display shall be limited to ±0.75 diopters to minimize focus-fixation mismatch.
requirements.site_hook: With eye-to-screen distance d (m), allowed virtual depth range is 1/(1/d ± 0.75) - computable from viewing distance

requirements.section_title: Virtual environments, remote, automated and unmanned systems
requirements.title: Monitoring task duration
requirements.text: The system should not require users to perform purely monitoring tasks for longer than 20 minutes at a time.
requirements.site_hook: Not geometric

requirements.section_title: Virtual environments, remote, automated and unmanned systems
requirements.title: UxV control latency limits
requirements.text: Table XXXVI latency limits (human-performed control): vehicle motion control 100 ms (air UAV/RPA), 250 ms (ground UGV); weapon system control 100 ms (air), 100 ms (ground). Underwater, surface, orbital: per good human engineering practice (no value).
requirements.site_hook: Spec entry

requirements.section_title: Virtual environments, remote, automated and unmanned systems
requirements.title: UxV manual handling affordances
requirements.text: Manual handling affordances shall be provided to assist the operator during launch and recovery as well as other mission phases specified.
requirements.site_hook: UxV mass + handle geometry vs lift/carry limits (5.20)

requirements.section_title: Virtual environments, remote, automated and unmanned systems
requirements.title: Telemedicine critical text size
requirements.text: Critical information displayed as text should be at least 1/150th of the maximum expected viewing distance; important but non-critical text at least 1/300th (5.12.6.5.1.7).
requirements.site_hook: Eye-to-display distance tool -> min text height = distance/150 (critical) or /300

requirements.title: Unobstructed round transfer workspace
requirements.text: Unobstructed workspace shall be provided for transferring rounds from outside the vehicle to the ready rack and from the ready rack to the breech; rounds stowed so the loader requires minimum movement (5.13.1.1.3).
requirements.site_hook: Loader posture/reach path between rack and breech objects; clearance check

requirements.title: Ammunition racks not impeding escape/controls/footing
requirements.text: Ammunition stowage racks, loaded or empty, shall not impede escape, obstruct access to controls, obscure displays, or interfere with crew footing; and shall allow removal/replacement without striking protrusions (5.13.1.1.7.1).
requirements.site_hook: Clearance checks between rack objects, egress paths and reach paths

requirements.title: Ready rack to breech channel
requirements.text: Where ready racks are to the rear of the gun breech, the channel between rack and breech shall accommodate the longest round anticipated plus the thickness of the 95th percentile male hand, including gloves or protection, plus an additional 50 mm (2 in) of clearance.

values.condition: = longest round length + P95 male hand thickness (gloved) + 50 mm (2 in)

requirements.site_hook: Distance rack-to-breech objects vs round length + hand thickness (survey P95 male) + glove + 50 mm
requirements.percentile_rule: 95th percentile male hand thickness, gloved

requirements.title: Spring-loaded round ejection travel
requirements.text: Floor and hull stowage tube-type ammunition racks shall be spring loaded so stowed rounds travel at least 50 mm (2 in) out of the rack when unlatched; if not feasible, tube end recessed for hand grip (5.13.1.1.7.4).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist

requirements.title: Upright ammunition floor retainer hand clearance
requirements.text: Upright-mounted ammunition weighing over 18.1 kg (40 lb) shall have a floor retainer with sufficient clearance to allow removal by the appropriate dimensions of the 95th percentile male hand, including gloves or protection.
requirements.site_hook: Retainer gap vs P95 male hand breadth/thickness + glove
requirements.percentile_rule: 95th percentile male hand, gloved

requirements.title: Ammunition rack latch force
requirements.text: Ammunition rack latching mechanisms shall be quick-release requiring no more than 53 newtons (12 pounds-force) to operate; free of sharp edges that can snag clothing (5.13.1.1.7.6.1).
requirements.site_hook: Force parameter

requirements.title: Fuze pointer to index separation
requirements.text: The pointer tip and index marks shall not be separated by more than 1.5 mm (0.06 in).

values.quantity: pointer tip to index mark gap

requirements.site_hook: Component detail

requirements.title: Breech manual removability mass
requirements.text: A breech weighing over 22.5 kg (50 lb) shall not be considered manually removable.
requirements.site_hook: Box/object mass vs lift limit

requirements.title: Manual breech operating force
requirements.text: For manual breech operation, the operating force shall not exceed 130 newtons (29 pounds-force) one-handed and 220 newtons (50 pounds-force) two-handed.
requirements.site_hook: Force parameter; compare

requirements.title: Primary armament chamber cleaning accommodation
requirements.text: The primary armament chamber shall be capable of being cleaned by the multivariate central 90 percent (95 percent preferred) of suitably clothed and equipped males and females of the target user population.
requirements.site_hook: Reach from standing/kneeling posture into chamber for smallest and largest users
requirements.percentile_rule: multivariate central 90% (95% preferred) of clothed/equipped males AND of females

requirements.title: Quadrant access through elevation range
requirements.text: Quadrants and other devices mounted on the primary armament shall be accessible to the gunner throughout the full range of elevation and depression.
requirements.site_hook: Reach from gunner seat to device position at min and max gun elevation

requirements.title: Secondary armament mounting from natural position
requirements.text: The secondary dismountable armament shall be capable of being mounted on the vehicle by crewmembers from a natural working position (not extending or contorting the body) with the weapon fully assembled.
requirements.site_hook: Posture analysis (RULA/REBA) with weapon mass at mount location; flag high scores

requirements.title: Rear sight notch width
requirements.text: The rear sight notch shall be 3 mm (0.12 in) or wider, and the front sight shall be wide enough to fill the notch when sighting.
requirements.site_hook: Weapon object parameter (sight geometry)

requirements.title: Weapon loading/charging accommodation
requirements.text: The weapon shall be capable of being loaded (in vehicle and ground mount) and charged (5.13.1.3.8.3) by the multivariate central 90 percent (95 percent preferred) of suitably clothed and equipped males and females.
requirements.site_hook: Reach + strength check across population for charging handle location
requirements.percentile_rule: multivariate central 90% (95% preferred) of clothed/equipped males AND of females

requirements.title: Charging in prone position
requirements.text: For ground mount weapons, charging shall be possible with the user in the prone position.
requirements.site_hook: Prone posture reach to charging handle object

requirements.title: Charging resistance
requirements.text: Charging resistance shall not exceed 340 newtons (250 pounds-force) breakout force or 80 newtons (60 pounds-force) sustained. [As printed: SI and customary values are inconsistent (340 N ≈ 76 lbf; 80 N ≈ 18 lbf).]
requirements.site_hook: Force parameter; compare; flag unit inconsistency

requirements.title: Remove jammed cases accommodation
requirements.text: Weapon design shall permit the central 90% (95% preferred) of clothed/equipped males and females to remove jammed cases without disassembly and without endangering the hand; ammunition chute openings large enough for this population to guide ammunition (5.13.1.3.8.11).
requirements.site_hook: Hand/finger dimension (gloved, P95M) vs opening sizes
requirements.percentile_rule: multivariate central 90% (95% preferred) of clothed/equipped males AND of females

requirements.title: Ammunition chute edge radius
requirements.text: Ammunition chutes shall be free of sharp edges; edges rounded to a radius not less than 0.75 mm (0.03 in) per 5.7.6.3.
requirements.site_hook: Edge radius parameter

requirements.title: Rate selector / safety size and resistance
requirements.text: Rate selectors and safeties shall be of sufficient size and resistance to accommodate the central 90% (95% preferred) of clothed/equipped males and females; detents for each position (5.13.1.3.8.15).
requirements.site_hook: Control size vs gloved finger dimensions
requirements.percentile_rule: multivariate central 90% (95% preferred) of clothed/equipped males AND of females

requirements.title: Small arms operable by population in any firing position
requirements.text: Weapons shall be designed so the multivariate central 90 percent (95 percent preferred) of suitably clothed and equipped males and females can perform all required tasks (field operation and maintenance) in daylight and at night from any operational firing position.
requirements.site_hook: Weapon object held in standing/kneeling/prone firing postures for each population case: check reach to trigger/controls and eye alignment with sight
requirements.percentile_rule: multivariate central 90% (95% preferred) of clothed/equipped males AND of females

requirements.title: Weapon contact surfaces smooth
requirements.text: Surfaces of the weapon contacting the user's body or clothing during firing or maneuvering shall be smooth with no sharp edges; heat-generating parts against skin insulated as directed (5.13.1.4.1.4).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist

requirements.title: Ambidextrous controls and safety
requirements.text: Weapon controls/latches should be ambidextrous and located to avoid unintentional actuation; the safety selector should be ambidextrous and operable SAFE/FIRE without moving either hand from its normal firing position (5.13.1.4.1.12).
requirements.site_hook: Thumb reach from firing grip to selector for small hand (P5F hand length) both hands
requirements.percentile_rule: small hand (P5F)

requirements.title: Face/eye safety during recoil
requirements.text: No part of the weapon shall endanger the user's face during firing when the head is in the proper eyesight position; no part of the scope shall endanger the user's eye during recoil (5.13.1.4.1.14.1).
requirements.site_hook: Distance eye-to-scope eyepiece >= recoil travel + eye relief (see 5.13.2.6)

requirements.title: Magazine one-hand insertion
requirements.text: Magazines shall be inserted with one hand, only in correct orientation (5.13.1.4.1.15), non-slip finish (5.13.1.4.1.15.2).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist

requirements.title: Bipod with arctic mittens
requirements.text: A user wearing arctic mittens shall be able to extend or retract the bipod; with bipod retracted, the user shall be able to grasp the foregrip without obstruction in any firing position (5.13.1.4.2.2.3).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist

requirements.title: Sight adjustments in mission clothing
requirements.text: Users wearing mission clothing and equipment shall be able to precisely set windage and elevation controls without tools; settings verifiable from firing position without moving body or weapon (5.13.1.4.2.3.7).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist

requirements.title: Spent case ejection direction
requirements.text: Weapons shall eject spent cases into the first quadrant (forward and to the right) as a default; where possible allow left-handed adjustment to second quadrant (forward and to the left).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist

requirements.title: Post-fire reacquisition time
requirements.text: The time lag for post-fire reacquisition tracking of the intended target should not exceed 5 seconds.
requirements.site_hook: Performance spec

requirements.title: Manual tracking crank speed and radius
requirements.text: Crank speed shall be from 140 to 200 RPM of the crank for radii between 55 and 115 mm (2.2 and 4.5 in). As crank radius increases, required RPM may decrease.
requirements.site_hook: Sandbox hand-wheel/crank object radius; compare 55-115 mm; RPM entered by user

requirements.title: Azimuth traverse rate by crank
requirements.text: Each full revolution of the manual crank shall equate to weapon movement such that the complete azimuth arc can be traversed at a steady rate of at least 22.5 degrees per second.
requirements.site_hook: Gear ratio x RPM entry

requirements.title: Elevation traverse time by crank
requirements.text: Complete traversing of the elevation arc from fully declined to fully inclined (or vice versa) shall be accomplished within 3 seconds.
requirements.site_hook: Gear ratio x RPM entry

requirements.title: Single integrated 2D tracking control
requirements.text: A single integrated control, rather than separate controls for each dimension, shall be used for two-dimensional tracking.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist

requirements.title: Tracking control hand/forearm support
requirements.text: Where a tracking control is used, a hand, wrist, or forearm support shall be provided.
requirements.site_hook: Armrest object near tracking control; check forearm contact in gunner posture

requirements.title: Optics viewing angle / no unusual posture
requirements.text: Optical systems shall preclude any design that forces the user to adopt unusual postures for an effective viewing angle.
requirements.site_hook: Place eye at eyepiece: posture analysis (neck flexion/extension, RULA/REBA) for all population cases; flag extreme joint angles
requirements.percentile_rule: full population range

requirements.title: Handheld rifle/pistol sight magnification
requirements.text: Magnification of unstabilized, unsupported, handheld rifle and pistol sights shall be not more than 4-power unless selectable magnification or stabilization is present.
requirements.site_hook: Optics spec

requirements.title: Handheld binocular magnification
requirements.text: Magnification of unstabilized, unsupported, handheld monoculars or binoculars shall be not more than 8-power.
requirements.site_hook: Optics spec

requirements.title: Exit pupil from objective / magnification
requirements.text: Objective lens diameter divided by the highest magnification shall give an exit pupil diameter no less than 2 mm (0.08 in) and should be 3 mm (0.12 in) or more; daylight exit pupil not less than 2 mm, should be 3 mm or more (5.13.2.5.2).
requirements.site_hook: Optics spec

requirements.title: Low-light exit pupil
requirements.text: For twilight and lower light levels, the exit pupil diameter shall be not less than 7 mm (0.28 in).
requirements.site_hook: Optics spec

requirements.title: Long eye relief for vehicle sights
requirements.text: A long eye relief (e.g., 90 mm [3.5 in]) shall be provided for vehicular mounted sights if the user must be protected from gun recoil, observe on the move, or maintain field-of-view while wearing a protective mask.

values.condition: example value 3.5 in; recoil / on the move / protective mask

requirements.site_hook: Eye point to eyepiece distance in gunner posture; compare >= 90 mm when flagged; check mask/helmet clearance

requirements.title: Eye relief for spectacle wearers
requirements.text: To permit use by users wearing glasses when recoil is not encountered, eye relief shall be not less than 15 mm (0.59 in).
requirements.site_hook: Eye-to-eyepiece distance; compare

requirements.title: Eyepiece dioptric adjustment
requirements.text: Fixed-focus eyepieces set between -0.50 and -1.00 diopter may be used for devices 4-power and less; over 4-power, dioptric adjustment -4.0 to +2.0 diopters required (-6.0 to +2.0 desired) marked in 0.5-diopter increments.
requirements.site_hook: Optics spec

requirements.title: Axial resolution
requirements.text: Axial resolution shall be equal to or better than 300 microradians (1 minute) divided by the magnification; luminous transmission not less than 50 percent (5.13.2.8.2).
requirements.site_hook: Optics spec

requirements.title: Biocular viewing for long low-light use
requirements.text: Where continuous use of a sight under low illumination will exceed one minute, a single optical train with two eyepieces shall be provided if this does not lead to unacceptable light losses.
requirements.site_hook: Optics spec

requirements.title: Binocular eyepiece separation (IPD range)
requirements.text: Binocular and biocular devices shall have an eyepiece separation scaled from 50 to 75 mm (2 to 3 in).
requirements.site_hook: Compare range with interpupillary distance P1F..P99M from survey data (ANSUR II has pupillary distance)

requirements.title: Valve criticality categories 1-3
requirements.text: Valves shall be rated by temporal and operational human factors criticality into three categories. Cat 1: critical for safety or operations; used at least once in a 6-month period for routine operation/maintenance; high likelihood of failure; or failure/lack of quick access could lead to injury, damage or degraded mission (e.g., control valves and bypasses/isolation, relief/depressurizing, trip and anti-surge, emergency shutdown, liquid cargo transfer, firefighting/damage control/propulsion/process/steering, time-constrained). Cat 2: not critical but required for routine operation and maintenance (e.g., sewage, condensate drain, service oil, potable water, ship service air, hydraulic service, defrost gas, normal startup/shutdown manual valves, no quick action, drain/vent with flange or cap, pressure test). Cat 3: used infrequently (dry dock, commissioning, decommissioning, startup after extended shutdown, extended shutdown, isolation for inspections, tie-in/hot-tap).

values.condition: used at least once in a 6-month period

requirements.site_hook: Valve object 'category' parameter (1/2/3) drives the location/height rules below.

requirements.site_hook: Checklist.

requirements.site_hook: Checklist.

requirements.title: PED mounting adjustability and stability
requirements.text: Mounting methods shall permit adjustment for comfortable carriage and secure mounting, and avoid excessive movement (bouncing/twisting) during walking, running, crawling, climbing, ingress, egress. Mounting shall be compatible with user environment such as vehicle or aircraft (5.19.2.3).

requirements.title: PED contact temperature
requirements.text: PEDs contacting the body shall maintain operating temperature at or below core body temperature of 37 degC (98.6 degF), consistent with 5.7.5.9. Heat shield required where skin temperature rise cannot be prevented (5.19.2.11.1.3); should not trap heat (5.19.2.11.2).

requirements.title: Strength and handling - holistic system approach
requirements.text: Requirements apply to all DoD personnel unless user population-specific strength data are specified (see 6.2). requirements.title: Strength not inferred from body size
requirements.text: Because of the low correlation between strength and size, size shall not be used to determine accommodation of strength and endurance; strength shall be considered separately. Members of minimum size are very unlikely also to have minimum strength.

requirements.title: Operability - accommodate weakest personnel
requirements.text: The strength and endurance performance characteristics of the weakest personnel performing the actual or equivalent task shall be accommodated. requirements.title: Load carriage - weight distribution over muscle groups
requirements.text: Individual portions of equipment shall be designed so that, when carried, the load weight is distributed effectively through as many appropriate muscle groups as possible.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item.

requirements.title: Load carriage - weight/distribution compatibility
requirements.text: Load-carrying systems shall be compatible with the weight and distribution of the items carried. Typical load for mission, climate and occupational specialty as specified (see 6.2).

requirements.title: Load carriage - quick-release
requirements.text: Load carrying systems shall be provided with a quick-release capability.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item.

requirements.text: 'Portable' refers to an item able to be carried a distance of not more than 2.1 kilometers (1.25 miles) by the number of personnel dictated by the weight of the item.

requirements.text: When necessary, lifting aids such as handles shall be provided to permit a second person to assist the individual carrying the load in placing the load on their body.

requirements.title: Backpacks over 20 kg - assist handles

requirements.title: Backpack load distribution
requirements.text: Backpacking aids shall distribute the load over as many muscle groups as possible by buttock and hip supports in addition to padded shoulder straps and a chest strap.

requirements.title: Backpack centre of gravity

requirements.title: Minimize chest/armpit pressure
requirements.text: Load-carrying design shall minimize pressure or compression to the chest or armpits.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item.

requirements.title: Transmit weight through bone
requirements.text: Load-carrying design shall eliminate local strain by transmitting weight to the ground through bone.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item.

requirements.title: Minimize pressure on sensitive tissues
requirements.text: Load carriage systems should minimize pressure over sensitive tissues such as breasts or superficial nerves (anterior/posterior shoulder over the brachial plexus).
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item.

requirements.title: Wide padded straps
requirements.text: Straps should be sufficiently wide and padded to distribute pressure and reduce compression forces.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item.

requirements.title: Aids not to interfere with movement
requirements.text: Aids shall not produce unbalanced loads, interfere with head movements, limit squatting, interfere with walking or climbing over low obstacles, interfere with shoulder girdle movement, strain shoulder muscle, compress blood vessels, cause static compression from lengthy sitting, or interfere with thermoregulation beyond the load's own effects.
requirements.site_hook: With a pack object attached, test squat/climb/head-rotation postures for collisions; rest checklist.

requirements.title: Body armor - freedom of movement
requirements.text: The load shall be designed to permit freedom of movement required to perform essential tasks.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist; could test ROM postures with armor volume.

requirements.title: Body armor - no sharp edges/projections
requirements.text: The load shall be free of sharp edges or projections that may harm the user or present a snag hazard; covers or cases may be provided.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item.

requirements.title: Body armor - shape not to interfere
requirements.text: Shape and weight of the load shall not interfere with normal loaded gait; head movements; raising/lowering the load over obstacles; seeing where the feet are placed when walking; squatting, kneeling or prone positions; thermoregulation; or normal posture.
requirements.site_hook: With armor/pack volume on mannequin: check line of sight to feet while walking, and squat/kneel/prone postures for interference.

requirements.title: Two-person carry - stretcher handles
requirements.text: Where the load is designed for carrying by two persons, a combination of stretcher-type handles and shoulder support shall be used, if feasible.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item.

requirements.title: Lifting limits - scope and exclusions
requirements.text: Lifting limits depend on posture relative to load, frequency and duration. Unless otherwise specified they accommodate the multivariate central 90 percent (95 percent preferred) of clothed/equipped males and females of the target population. They do NOT apply to: lifting outside a stationary location, holding more than 3 seconds, one-handed lifting, lifting with hands and other body parts (shoulder or leg), lifting more than 8 hours, lifting seated or kneeling, restricted space, unstable surface, while operating equipment, high speed (faster than 75 cm/s [30 in/s]), slippery floors (<0.4 coefficient of friction sole-floor), and cold or hot environments (outside temperature 19 to 26 degC [66 to 79 degF]). Generally not applicable to unbalanced load or posture (biomechanical analysis recommended). The limits apply to objects that weigh more than 2.3 kg (5 lb).

values.quantity: object mass for lifting limits to apply

values.condition: 30 in/s; faster is out of scope

values.quantity: sole-floor coefficient of friction within scope

requirements.site_hook: Lifting calculator should validate inputs: two-handed, standing (not seated/kneeling), mass > 2.3 kg, speed <= 75 cm/s, COF >= 0.4, temp 19-26 degC, else warn 'outside NIOSH scope'.
requirements.percentile_rule: multivariate central 90% (95% preferred) of clothed/equipped males and of females of target population

requirements.title: Maximum allowable weight - single lifter (load constant)
requirements.text: The maximum allowable weight limit for a single lifter is 23 kg (51 lb) for two-handed lifting in the ideal lifting condition (see 5.20.3.3).
requirements.site_hook: Sandbox box mass vs 23 kg absolute cap; actual cap is WL from 5.20.3.3.

requirements.title: Two-person lifting
requirements.text: Double the weight limits (determined in 5.20.3.3) shall be used as the maximum design weight for items requiring two-person lifting, provided the load is uniformly distributed between the two lifters.

values.condition: 2 x single-person WL; load uniformly distributed

requirements.site_hook: Team-lift option in lifting calculator: limit = 2 x WL.

requirements.title: Three or more lifters
requirements.text: Where three or more persons lift simultaneously, not more than 75 percent of the one-person value should be added for each additional lifter, provided the object is large enough that lifters do not interfere and each can attain a secure grip.

values.condition: 3+ lifters; no interference; secure grip each

requirements.site_hook: Lifting calculator: limit(n) = WL*(2 + 0.75*(n-2)).

requirements.title: Maximum design weight limits by number of lifters
requirements.text: Maximum design weight limit: 1 lifter 23 kg (51 lb); 2 lifters 46 kg (102 lb); 3 lifters 63 kg (140 lb); 4 lifters 81 kg (178 lb); 5 lifters 98 kg (216 lb); 6 lifters 115 kg (254 lb).
requirements.site_hook: Lookup by team size in lifting calculator / box object 'lifters' parameter.

requirements.title: Multi-person lifting teams - conditions
requirements.text: Multi-person teams may be used when the object's weight is evenly distributed and fair or better coupling is achievable. An even number of members should be assigned (2, 4, or 6). Whenever possible no more than four lifters should be assigned to a team.
requirements.site_hook: Warn if team size odd or > 4, or coupling = poor.

requirements.title: Maximum number of lifters from object perimeter
requirements.text: Maximum permissible number of lifters = perimeter of object in cm / 60 (inches / 24), rounded to the nearest whole number. Example: 62 cm x 88 cm: (2 x 62 + 2 x 88)/60 [(2 x 25 + 2 x 35)/24] = 5 lifters.
requirements.site_hook: Box object length/width -> perimeter -> n_max; compare to assigned team size.

requirements.title: Lifting equation (maximum weight limit WL)
requirements.text: WL = LC x HM x VM x DM x AM x FM x CM, where LC (load constant) = 23 kg (51 lb), HM horizontal multiplier, VM vertical multiplier, DM distance multiplier, AM asymmetry multiplier, FM frequency multiplier (table XLV), CM coupling multiplier (table XLVI). In the ideal lifting condition all multipliers are 1.0; otherwise multipliers < 1.0 reduce WL.
requirements.site_hook: Implement in posture analysis for lifting postures: H, V from hand/box CG vs mid-point between inner ankle bones; D from origin/destination V; A from trunk-to-load angle; F, duration, coupling entered by user; compare box mass to min(WL_origin, WL_destination).
requirements.percentile_rule: multivariate central 90% (95% preferred) of clothed/equipped males and of females of target population

requirements.title: Formulas for lifting multipliers
requirements.text: Metric (cm): HM = 25/H; VM = 1 - (0.003|V-75|); DM = 0.82 + (4.5/D); AM = 1 - (0.0032A) (A in degrees); FM from table XLV; CM from table XLVI. US customary (in): HM = 10/H; VM = 1 - (0.0075|V-30|); DM = 0.82 + (1.8/D); AM = 1 - (0.0032A). Notes: sourced from Applications Manual for the Revised NIOSH Lifting Equation; multipliers may not exceed 1.0 - values > 1.0 are set to 1.0 (e.g., D = 10 cm gives 0.82+(4.5/10) = 1.27, so DM = 1.0).

values.condition: metric: 25/H (H in cm); customary: 10/H (H in in)

requirements.site_hook: Clamp each multiplier to max 1.0. NOTE: Table XLII prints no lower cut-offs for H, V, D, A (the NIOSH manual uses H 25-63 cm, V 0-175 cm, D 25-175 cm, A 0-135 deg) - site should not invent them, but may warn that values outside NIOSH ranges are unvalidated.

requirements.title: Definitions of lifting task variables (H, V, D, A)
requirements.text: H = distance between the floor projection of the load CG and the projection of the person's CG (figures 98/99: measured from the mid-point between the inner ankle bones to the point of projection of the load). V = vertical distance from load CG to the floor. D = vertical travel distance between origin and destination. A = angular displacement of the load from the sagittal line (asymmetry angle between sagittal line and asymmetry line, figure 99).
requirements.site_hook: Geometry: H = horizontal distance (top view) from midpoint of inner ankle bones to box CG projection; V = box CG height above floor; A = angle between mannequin sagittal line and line from ankle midpoint to load projection.

requirements.title: Evaluate lift at origin and destination
requirements.text: Task variables are measured at the origin and destination of the lift; where control at the destination gives two weight limits, the lower of the two should be used as the design guideline for the entire lift.
requirements.site_hook: Compute WL for both lift-origin and lift-destination postures; report min.

requirements.title: Graphic representation of task variables H and V
requirements.text: Figure shows V as vertical distance from floor to hands/load and H as horizontal distance from the mid-point between inner ankle bones to the point of projection of the load (top view: horizontal and lateral axes). No numeric limits in figure.
requirements.site_hook: Reference geometry for H and V measurement.

requirements.title: Graphic representation of task variable A
requirements.text: Figure shows sagittal and frontal planes; asymmetric angle A is the angle between the sagittal line and the asymmetry line (from mid-point between inner ankle bones to point of projection of load). No numeric limits.
requirements.site_hook: Reference geometry for A measurement.

requirements.title: Lifting duration categories
requirements.text: Lifting duration is classified as short-duration (less than 1 hour), moderate-duration (1 to 2 hours), and long-duration (2 to 8 hours), based on pattern of continuous work-time and recovery-time (non-lifting light work).
requirements.site_hook: User selects work duration category for FM lookup.

requirements.title: Lifting duration category and required rest
requirements.text: Short: t <= 1 hour, required resting period >=100% of duration of continuous lifting task. Moderate: 1 hour < t <= 2 hours, >=30% of continuous lifting task. Long: 2 hours < t <= 8 hours, no amount specified. If sufficient rest is not provided, the next higher category is used for the frequency multiplier.

values.condition: Short; rest >= 100% of continuous lifting duration
Long (2 h < t <= 8 h); no rest specified

requirements.site_hook: User inputs duration and rest; bump category if rest insufficient.

requirements.title: Frequency multiplier inputs and 15 lifts/min cap
requirements.text: FM depends on lifts per minute (F), work duration (WD) and vertical height V. F = average lifts/min over a 15-minute period. If infrequent, F = number of lifts / 8 (or work hours a day); if F < 0.2 use 0.2. A lifting task shall not be designed to have a lifting frequency greater than 15 lifts per minute.
requirements.site_hook: User enters F; validate <= 15; floor at 0.2.

requirements.title: Frequency multipliers (FM)
requirements.site_hook: Lookup table in lifting calculator (user enters F and WD; V from geometry). Table gives discrete F only - no interpolation rule printed.

requirements.title: Coupling classification
requirements.text: Coupling shall be classified as good, fair, or poor. Good: power grips usable with both hands (e.g., box with cutout handles). Fair: power grips not possible but fingers can flex to form a 90-degree angle. Poor: all other. If one hand is fair and the other good, use fair.

values.condition: fingers able to flex to 90 deg under load

requirements.site_hook: Box object parameter: coupling (good/fair/poor) or handles/cutouts flag.

requirements.title: Coupling multiplier (CM)
requirements.text: Good: 1.00 (V < 75 cm [30 in]), 1.00 (V >= 75 cm [30 in]). Fair: 0.95 (V < 75 cm), 1.00 (V >= 75 cm). Poor: 0.90, 0.90. Sourced from the Revised NIOSH Lifting Equation Applications Manual.
requirements.site_hook: Lookup by coupling and V class.

requirements.title: Carrying limits - scope, power grips, body-worn load
requirements.text: Carrying limits apply to lifting and carrying for more than 1 m (3.3 ft); based on psychophysical data for multivariate central 90 percent (95 percent preferred) of males and females. Power grips for carrying shall be provided (e.g., handles for boxes or totes). Limits apply to objects grasped with the hands, not body-borne items. Limits may be reduced when body armor/worn equipment exceeds 9 kg (20 lb); if load carriage weighs more than 9 kg (20 lb), a biomechanical analysis and energy expenditure estimation shall be performed. Lifting limits at the origin (before carrying) and destination (after carrying) shall be determined, and the lowest of the three limits used.

values.quantity: carry distance for carrying limits to apply

requirements.site_hook: Carry calculator: WL_carry = min(WL_lift_origin, Table XLVII, WL_lift_destination); flag if worn load > 9 kg.
requirements.percentile_rule: multivariate central 90% (95% preferred) of clothed/equipped males and of females of target population

requirements.title: Two-person carry
requirements.text: Double the carrying weight limit shall be used as the maximum design weight for items requiring two-person carrying, provided the load is uniformly distributed.
requirements.site_hook: Team carry option: limit x 2.

requirements.title: More than two-person carry
requirements.text: Where three or more persons carry a load, not more than 75 percent of the one-person value may be added for each additional person, provided the object is large enough that workers do not interfere.
requirements.site_hook: Team carry calculator.

requirements.title: Carrying method - load height and upright torso; carts
requirements.text: Load should be grasped with both hands as close to the body as possible at a vertical height between the middle of the carrier's thighs and the bottom of the ribcage. The carrier shall keep the torso as upright as possible. A cart or other assist device is recommended for loads greater than 7 kg (15 lb) transported more than 15 m (50 ft).

values.condition: between mid-thigh and bottom of ribcage of the carrier

requirements.site_hook: Carrying posture: check box CG height between mannequin mid-thigh height and lower-rib (ribcage bottom) height at chosen percentile; report trunk flexion angle; recommend cart if mass > 7 kg and distance > 15 m.

requirements.title: Labeling of heavy items; hoist points
requirements.text: Items weighing more than the one-person lift or carry limit shall be prominently labeled with the weight of the object and lift limitation (e.g., mechanical, two-person lift, three-person lift). Where mechanical or power lift is required, hoist and lift points shall be provided and clearly labeled (see 5.4.10.4).

requirements.title: Load assistance devices - workspace design factors
requirements.text: Workplace design for two-wheeled hand trucks and four-wheeled dollies should consider coefficient of friction (static, dynamic, rolling), surface smoothness, and push/pull distance. Selection factors (5.20.5.1): worker body weight and strength, height/direction/distance from body of force application, posture, duration and distance, expected load, wheel/caster type; pushing preferable to pulling; casters maintained.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist; posture analysis can report hand height and trunk lean for push tasks.

requirements.title: Hand trucks/dollies - maximum incline
requirements.text: Dollies and hand trucks shall not be used to move loads up and down stairs or ramps with an angle of inclination greater than 7 degrees.
requirements.site_hook: Sandbox stairs/ramp angle: flag dolly/hand-truck route if > 7 deg (stairs always exceed).

requirements.title: Hand truck turning radius
requirements.text: Turning radius for hand trucks shall be not greater than 120 cm (48 in).
requirements.site_hook: Would need hand-truck object with turning radius parameter.

requirements.title: Dolly casters
requirements.text: Dollies shall have swivel casters at the handle end. Larger diameter wheels are easier to push.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist item.

requirements.title: Clear space for dollies/hand trucks
requirements.text: When dollies or hand trucks are required, clear space shall be provided within the area of their use.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist; no numeric value.

requirements.title: Exoskeletons - per ASTM standards
requirements.text: Use, characteristics and handling of exoskeletons shall be in accordance with ASTM F3323, ASTM F3444/F3444M, ASTM F3358, ASTM F3392, ASTM F3427.
requirements.site_hook: Out of scope for geometry checks.

requirements.title: Patient movement devices - best practices
requirements.text: Push rather than pull and use two hands; do not exceed equipment capacity; keep arms close and push with the whole body; remove unnecessary objects; avoid obstacles; plan path around furniture, doorways, sharp turns, thresholds, slopes; use powered devices when practical; remove defective equipment; maintain equipment, wheels and wheel locks.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist / guidance.

requirements.title: Push/pull tasks should be assessed
requirements.text: Pushing and pulling tasks should be assessed to determine whether they are safe manually; evidence-based recommendations should be used to determine whether assistive technology is needed.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist.

requirements.title: Horizontal push/pull force limits
requirements.text: Manual horizontal push and pull forces applied initially to set an object in motion or sustained over a short period shall not exceed the values of table XLVIII, as applicable, or table XLIX if more appropriate to the task.
requirements.site_hook: User enters required force and condition; compare to Table XLVIII / XLIX.

requirements.title: Horizontal push and pull forces (intermittent/short)
requirements.text: 66 N (15 lb) push or pull, both hands or one shoulder or the back, low traction 0.2 < mu < 0.3. 130 N (30 lb) push or pull, both hands/one shoulder/back, medium traction mu ~ 0.6. 160 N (36 lb) push, one hand, if braced against a vertical wall 50 to 150 cm (20 to 60 in) from and parallel to the push panel. 200 N (45 lb) push or pull, both hands/one shoulder/back, high traction mu > 0.9. 330 N (75 lb) push or pull, both hands/one shoulder/back, if braced against a vertical wall 50 to 175 cm (20 to 70 in) from and parallel to the panel or if anchoring the feet on a perfectly non-slip ground (like a footrest). 500 N (110 lb) push, the back, same bracing condition (50 to 175 cm [20 to 70 in]) or footrest. Footnotes: may be doubled for two and tripled for three users pushing simultaneously; for the fourth and each additional user not more than 75% of their push capability shall be added. Static COF for starting, dynamic COF for keeping motion. Note: values predicated on a vertical rough surface approximately 40 cm (16 in) wide and 50 to 125 cm (20 to 50 in) above the floor for force application with hands, shoulder or back.

requirements.title: Vertical push/pull force limits
requirements.text: Manual vertical push and pull forces required shall not exceed the applicable 5th percentile peak or mean force values of table XLIX or those given on figure 23 if more appropriate.
requirements.site_hook: Required vertical force vs Table XLIX P5 (female, as weakest) mean/peak for matching posture.
requirements.percentile_rule: 5th percentile

requirements.title: Means for handling
requirements.text: All items designed to be carried or removed and replaced shall have handles or other means for grasping, handling and carrying, where appropriate usable by a gloved or mittened hand.
requirements.site_hook: Box/equipment object flag 'has handles'.

requirements.title: Two handles
requirements.text: Items requiring handling shall be provided with not less than two handles or one handle and one grasp area.
requirements.site_hook: Box object 'handle count' >= 2.

requirements.title: Light items exempt
requirements.text: Unless otherwise specified, items weighing less than 4.5 kg (10 lb) whose form factor permits easy handling are exempt from the handle requirement.

values.condition: 10 lb; below this exempt if easily handled

requirements.site_hook: Skip handle check if box mass < 4.5 kg.

requirements.title: Handle location above CG
requirements.text: Handles, grasp areas, or hoist points shall be located above the center of gravity and so as to preclude uncontrolled swinging or tilting when lifted.
requirements.site_hook: Box object: compare handle attachment height with object CG height.

requirements.title: Handle clearance from obstructions
requirements.text: Handles, grasp areas, or hoist points shall provide at least 5 cm (2 in) of clearance from obstructions during handling.
requirements.site_hook: Clearance measurement between handle and nearby sandbox objects.

requirements.title: Handle location not to interfere
requirements.text: Handle location shall not interfere with installing, removing, operating, or maintaining the equipment.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist.

requirements.title: Non-fixed handle stop position
requirements.text: Non-fixed handles (hinged or foldout) shall have a stop position holding the handle perpendicular to the mounting surface.

values.quantity: handle stop angle to mounting surface

requirements.site_hook: Checklist.

requirements.title: Non-fixed handle one-hand deploy
requirements.text: Non-fixed handles shall be capable of being placed into carrying position by one hand, and where appropriate by a gloved or mittened hand.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist.

requirements.title: Non-slip bottom grasp surface
requirements.text: Where the bottom surface is used as a handhold during removal or installation, a non-slip grasp surface (grooved, knurled, or frictional) shall be provided.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist.

requirements.title: Handle dimensions per figure 101
requirements.text: Handles used with mittened, gloved, or ungloved hands shall meet the minimum applicable dimensions shown on figure 101.

requirements.text: Force requirements to operate handles and grasp areas other than controls covered by 5.1 shall not exceed the values on figure 23.

requirements.title: Handle material not conductive
requirements.text: Handles or grasp areas used with bare hands shall have surfaces that are not thermally (see 5.7.5.9) or electrically conductive.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist.

requirements.title: Handle surface hardness
requirements.text: Surface shall be sufficiently hard to prevent embedding of grit and grime during normal use.
requirements.site_hook: Checklist.

requirements.title: Handle shape for frequent/long carrying
requirements.text: Handles shaped to be held by the hand (e.g., one-hand bar or T-bar) shall be used when items must be carried frequently or for long periods.

requirements.title: Acquisition parameters the procuring activity sets
requirements.text: Acquisition documents should specify (among others): target user population accommodation (4.5.3), PPE (4.11), sub-population accommodation (5.8.2.3), accommodation if other than specified (5.8.3.1, 5.8.3.2, 5.10.1), anthropometric database(s) (5.8.4.2.2), boot measurements with PPE (5.10.2.4.2), work bench/desk heights (5.10.3.9.2.2), armrest adjustability (5.10.3.12.11), physical space in equipment (5.11.2.7.1), maximum weight for the smallest female (5.7.2.6.3).
